data.title: Follower (Cap 1)
data.body: A novice helper who provides basic assistance. Loyalty and Fitness states apply.

data.title: Follower (Cap 2)
data.body: A competent assistant who provides reliable support. Loyalty and Fitness states apply.

data.title: Follower (Cap 3)
data.body: A skilled specialist who provides valuable aid. Loyalty and Fitness states apply.

data.title: Follower (Cap 4)
data.body: An expert ally who provides significant capability. Can be delegated Assets. Loyalty and Fitness states apply.

data.title: Follower (Cap 5)
data.body: A master companion with exceptional ability. Can be delegated Assets. Loyalty and Fitness states apply.

data.title: Major Asset
data.body: A large enterprise, fortress, or regional authority. Activation: spend 1 Boon for scene impact.

data.title: Minor Asset
data.body: A small resource such as a safehouse, workshop, or minor contact network. Activation: spend 1 Boon for scene impact.

data.title: Standard Asset
data.body: A significant resource such as a guild membership, trading post, or spy network. Activation: spend 1 Boon for scene impact.

data.title: War Mount Asset
data.body: A trained combat mount (warhorse, dune-strider, etc.). Increases overland travel speed and endurance. With Cavalier talent: +2d melee when moving Far→Near, +2d ranged when moving Near→Far.

data.title: Action Economy
data.body: Each turn: 1 Action and 1 Move. Move shifts one range band (Close ↔ Near ↔ Far). Actions include Attack, Disengage, Dash, Charge (full turn, costs 1 Fatigue), Skirmish (full turn, costs 1 Fatigue), Observe, Setup, Assist, Protect, Interact, Defend. Opportunity attacks occur when leaving Close without Disengage.

data.title: Adaptive Guard
data.body: When you take the Defend action, you may declare your defense pool after the GM calls Position. Once per scene, choose the pool after seeing the roll result.

data.title: Armored Fence
data.body: When you form a line with at least two other cataphracts, your unit gains +1 Armor and cannot be charged without the enemy first testing Resolve (DV 5). Breaking the formation costs 1 Fatigue. Requires Cataphract Charge, Heavy Armor Training.

data.title: Assassin's Mark
data.body: Once per scene, when you attack a target while Hidden, you may declare an Assassin's Mark. You gain +1 Harm and ignore 1 point of Armor (stacks with Backstab and Called Shot). If the attack is a Critical Hit and the target is not a boss-tier enemy, they are instantly incapacitated. After the attack, you may immediately make a Stealth test (DV 3) to re-enter stealth. Cost: marks 1 Fatigue and consumes your movement for the turn. Requires Tier II, Stealth 3+, Backstab, Shadow Dance.

data.title: Backstab
data.body: When attacking from stealth, deal +1 Harm and ignore 1 point of Armor. Once per scene. Requires Stealth 2+.

data.title: Battlefield Mastery
data.body: When engaged with 3+ opponents for 3 exchanges: melee attacks +1 Effect, enemies -1 die, your Position improves by one step, and you may convert one Harm 1 per exchange to Fatigue. Once per scene.

data.title: Battlefield Terror
data.body: Enemies in Close range act at -1 die due to intimidation. Once per scene, convert an enemy's success to a partial with cost.

data.title: Berserker Rage
data.body: Once per scene, for 3 rounds: +2 dice melee, ignore first Harm 1 each round, ignore Harm/Fatigue penalties, Position becomes Desperate. When rage ends, mark Fatigue equal to Spirit. Cannot be ended early.

data.title: Blade Dance
data.body: Once per scene, engage and attack up to 3 targets in one action. Each attack at -1 die, but your Position improves by one step. Requires Melee 5+, Duelist's Edge, Flurry Strike.

data.title: Called Shot
data.body: Once per scene, declare a Called Shot against an Unaware or aimed target; on hit, deal +1 Harm, ignore 1 Armor, and choose a condition (Blind, Disarm, Hamstring, Vitals). On miss, you are Exposed. Requires Ranged 2+.

data.title: Cataphract Charge
data.body: Once per scene, when you charge with a kontos lance, your attack ignores 1 point of Armor and, on a hit, the target must test Resolve (DV 4) or be Shaken (–1 die to all actions for one exchange). Requires Heavy Armor Training, Weapon Mastery (lance).

data.title: Cavalier
data.body: While mounted: +2 dice to melee attacks when moving Far→Near, or +2 dice to ranged attacks when moving Near→Far. Requires War Mount Asset.

data.title: Combat Reflexes
data.body: +1 DV on defense when surprised or flanked.

data.title: Curved Blade
data.body: Your saber's curved edge is designed for slashing while riding past. When you make a melee attack from horseback and continue moving, your attack gains +1 die and, on a hit, you may move an additional Near distance after the strike. Requires Weapon Mastery (saber), Mounted Charger.

data.title: Deathblow
data.body: Once per scene, when you make a melee attack from stealth and score a Critical Hit (a roll of 10 counts as two successes), you may declare a Deathblow. The target is immediately reduced to Harm 3 (incapacitated) if they are not a boss-tier enemy (GM discretion). If they are a boss-tier enemy, the attack instead deals +2 Harm and ignores an additional 1 point of Armor. Cost: marks 1 Fatigue. If the target survives, you are revealed and cannot re-enter stealth until the end of your next turn. Requires Tier II, Melee 3+.

data.title: Defensive Survival
data.body: +1 to defense DV while engaged in melee. Once per scene, convert first Harm 1 from melee to Fatigue.

data.title: Deflect Projectiles
data.body: When targeted by a ranged physical attack, roll Melee vs DV 3 to reduce or negate Harm.

data.title: Draconic Breath
data.body: Once per session, unleash a Breath Attack as a risky or desperate action. Gain +2 Effect against a group or large target when you do so. After using it, mark +2 Fatigue. If this would cause overflow, the GM instead marks +1 SB and you gain a new visible draconic mutation (eyes, scales, voice, or other change). Requires Dragonfolk origin, Tier II+.

data.title: Duelist's Edge
data.body: When engaged with a single opponent, +1 die to all melee rolls. Once per scene, ignore first Harm 1 or 2 from that opponent.

data.title: Effortless Charge
data.body: Ignore the Fatigue cost of Charge once per scene.

data.title: Effortless Skirmish
data.body: Ignore the Fatigue cost of Skirmish once per scene.

data.title: Elephant Charge
data.body: Once per scene, your elephant may make a trample attack against all enemies in a Near zone. Each target must test Body + Athletics (DV 4) or take Harm 2 and be knocked prone. Using this ability costs 2 Fatigue for the elephant. Requires Mahout's Bond.

data.title: Elusive Dodge
data.body: Once per exchange, when targeted by a physical attack, enter Defend stance as a free reaction. Mark 1 Fatigue after use.

data.title: Feigned Flight
data.body: Once per scene, you may pretend to retreat, luring an enemy into pursuit. Make a Deception test (DV 3). On a success, the enemy pursues, and on their next turn they must move toward you. On your following turn, you may turn and attack with +2 dice. This ability costs 1 Fatigue. Requires Light Cavalry, Deception 2+.

data.title: Fist of the Mountain
data.body: Once per session, your unarmed strike becomes a cataclysmic blow. Deal +4 Harm, ignore all Armor, and the target is knocked back two range bands and stunned (loses next action). After the blow, you suffer 2 Fatigue from the strain. Requires Iron Fist Technique, Inevitable Strike, Body 5+.

data.title: Flowing Spirit Technique
data.body: Convert up to 1 Harm into Fatigue per attack; +1 die against fear or charm effects.

data.title: Flurry Strike
data.body: Once per scene, make 2 attacks as one action, each at -1 die. Requires Melee 3+.

data.title: Furusiyya Training
data.body: You have trained in the full art of the horse warrior: lance, saber, bow, and horsemanship. You gain +1 die to all Ride tests and may re-roll one failed attack with a lance or saber per scene. Requires Weapon Mastery (lance or saber), Desert Rider.

data.title: Glancing Failure
data.body: When an enemy's attack against you results in a Partial, you may improve your Position by one step on your next action. Requires Body 2+, Spirit 2+.

data.title: Harassing Skirmish
data.body: Once per round, when you throw a javelin and then move away, your target suffers –1 die to their next action (distracted by the near miss). Requires Light Cavalry, Weapon Mastery (javelin).

data.title: High Stance Duelist
data.body: While Defending, enemies suffer -1 die to attacks against you; on a Success, your riposte becomes Dominant instead of Controlled.

data.title: Horse Archer's Art
data.body: Treat Mounted Archery penalties as eliminated for walk/trot; gallop/evade penalty is -1 die instead of -2. Once per scene, Skirmish while mounted allows an extra band of movement. Requires Mounted Archery. Cultural Affinity: Ykrul and Kuvani characters may reduce cost to 4 XP.

data.title: Howdah Archery
data.body: You may fire a bow or throw a javelin from the howdah without penalty, even while the elephant is moving. Additionally, you gain +1 Armor while in the howdah (cover). Requires Mahout's Bond, Ranged 2+.

data.title: Inevitable Strike
data.body: +2 dice to unarmed attacks; ignore 1 Armor; may counterattack when an enemy misses. Requires Iron Fist Technique + Perfect Timing Technique.

data.title: Iron Fist Technique
data.body: +1 die to unarmed attacks; strikes count as enchanted for harming supernatural creatures. Requires Disciplined Body.

data.title: Javelin Volley
data.body: Once per scene, you carry four javelins. As an action, you may throw two of them at the same target. Resolve each attack separately. After the volley, you are unarmed until you retrieve more javelins. Requires Weapon Mastery (javelins).

data.title: Khopesh Hook
data.body: Once per scene, when you attack with a khopesh, you may declare a hook attempt. Make a normal attack roll. On a hit, you may choose to forgo damage and instead disarm the target or pull them off balance (–1 die to their next action). Requires Weapon Mastery (khopesh or light blades).

data.title: Kontos Thrust
data.body: The kontos lance is held with two hands and braced against the horse's neck. You may use it one-handed while carrying a shield, but your attack suffers –1 die. If you use it two-handed, you gain +1 die and +1 Harm, but cannot use a shield. Requires Weapon Mastery (lance).

data.title: Lance Couch
data.body: Once per scene, when you charge with a lance and hit, your target must test Body + Endurance (DV 4) or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, your next attack against them gains +1 die. Requires Weapon Mastery (lance), Mounted Charger.

data.title: Lance Recover
data.body: After impaling an enemy with your lance, you may recover the weapon as a free action (you have trained to brace, strike, and withdraw in one motion). If you fail to recover, you must draw your saber.

data.title: Miststep Reflex
data.body: You are always treated as Defending against physical attacks unless Exposed, Grappled, or Surprised. If you take the Defend action, improve Position by +2 steps instead. Once per scene when you roll 1s while defending, you must mark 2 Fatigue or lose the benefit for the scene. Requires Elusive Dodge, Tier III, Stealth 4+, Athletics 3+.

data.title: Mystic Bulwark
data.body: When you Defend, you may Shield an adjacent ally (they gain your Position bonus). Once per scene, spend 2 Fatigue to extend to all allies in Near.

data.title: Perfect Timing Technique
data.body: Twice per scene, improve Position by +1 step; +1 die to reaction rolls.

data.title: Precise Strike
data.body: Once per scene, ignore armor on one attack if you had Dominant or Controlled position.

data.title: Relentless
data.body: May Charge or Skirmish over difficult terrain (Fatigue cost still applies).

data.title: Riposte Instinct
data.body: When you Defend and score a Success, you may make a free Melee attack against the attacker at Position -1. Once per scene.

data.title: Shadow Dance
data.body: After successfully hitting from stealth, you may attempt to re-enter stealth (Stealth test DV 3) as a free action.

data.title: Shrike Parry
data.body: When Defending against a melee attack: on Success, negate hit and make free attack; on Partial, reduce Harm by two levels; on Miss, improve Position next turn.

data.title: Stalwart's Ledger
data.body: When an enemy's attack against you results in a Miss, you may reposition one range band without provoking opportunity attacks. Once per scene.

data.title: Stampede
data.body: Once per session, you may send your elephant into a stampede. All enemies in a Large zone must test Spirit + Resolve (DV 5) or flee in panic. Those who fail also take Harm 1 (trampled). After the stampede, your elephant is Winded (–1 die on all actions for the rest of the scene). Requires Elephant Charge, Mahout's Bond.

data.title: Stubborn Pursuer
data.body: When an opponent Disengages, you may use your reaction to move with them, staying in Close range. Once per round.

data.title: Tactical Movement
data.body: Move within engagement zone as a Move action (instead of full action). Once per scene, disengage from Close as a Move action.

data.title: The Hollow Lance
data.body: Once per session, your lance is made of a hollow tube that whistles when thrown. You may throw your lance as a ranged weapon (Near range). On a hit, the target is Shaken (–1 die to all actions) for one exchange, and the whistling sound panics nearby horses (they must test Resolve or flee). Requires Lance Recover, Weapon Mastery (lance).

data.title: The Miss That Feeds
data.body: When an enemy's attack against you results in a Miss, you gain +1 Position on your next action against that enemy. Requires Body 2+.

data.title: Transcendent Harmony
data.body: Convert 2 Harm into Fatigue; once per session become immune to Harm; allies gain +1 defense. Requires Flowing Spirit Technique + Perfect Timing Technique, Spirit 4+.

data.title: Untouchable Form
data.body: +1 die to unarmed attacks; convert 2 Harm into Fatigue; cannot be grappled. Requires Iron Fist Technique + Flowing Spirit Technique.

data.title: Wardbreaker Reflex
data.body: When Defending against spells or supernatural effects, reroll 1 failed die; if it succeeds, mark +1 Fatigue.

data.title: Way of the Empty Mind
data.body: Immune to fear effects and magical mind-reading. +2 dice to resist charm or mind control. Requires Spirit 3+ and Meditative Focus.

data.title: Weapon Mastery
data.body: Choose a weapon type; gain +2 dice when using it. Once per scene, +1 Effect with signature weapon.

data.title: Weapon Training
data.body: +1 die with a chosen weapon category (instead of +2 from the Major version).

data.title: Whirlwind Kick
data.body: Once per scene, make an unarmed attack against all enemies in Close range. Roll once, compare to each target's defense. Requires Iron Fist Technique.

data.title: Buckler
data.body: Small shield. +1d to Defend actions once per scene. Off-hand occupied; -1d to ranged attacks.

data.title: Heater Shield
data.body: Standard shield. +1d to Defend actions; 1 Harm → Fatigue per scene. Off-hand occupied; -1d to ranged attacks.

data.title: Heavy Armor
data.body: Heavy plate. Conversion: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Fatigue 2.

data.title: Heavy Weapon
data.body: Punishing, slow. Harm 3. Close: -1d, Near: +3d. Tempo: Slow. Long enough to also threaten the Reach band (+0d) in tables using the extended 5-band range tracker (see Range Bands); blocked at Far and Absent.

data.title: Light Armor
data.body: Light flexible armor. Conversion: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Harm 1 + Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Harm 2 + Fatigue 1.

data.title: Light Weapon
data.body: Fast, concealable. Harm 1. Close: +2d, Near: +1d. Tempo: Fast. Too short to threaten Reach, Far, or Absent in tables using the extended 5-band range tracker (see Range Bands).

data.title: Medium Armor
data.body: Balanced protection. Conversion: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Harm 2 + Fatigue 1.

data.title: Medium Weapon
data.body: Balanced, battlefield standard. Harm 2. Close: +1d, Near: +2d. Tempo: Standard. Not quite long enough to threaten Reach in tables using the extended 5-band range tracker (see Range Bands); blocked at Reach, Far, and Absent.

data.title: Pavise
data.body: Large shield. Plant to create heavy cover (one direction). Bulky; cannot move while planted.

data.title: The Hollow
data.body: The Hollow is the unpaid interest of every broken promise, erased name, or unsettled debt. It exists in gaps: the ninth step that isn't there, the ninth cup not poured. It does not hate—it remembers. It appears as Oath-Keepers, Still Voices, and other manifestations of forgotten obligation.

data.title: The Ninth Taboo
data.body: The wise stop at eight: eight breaths, eight bells, eight cups. The ninth is the Hollow's share. To count to nine, speak the ninth name, or pour the ninth cup is to invite the Hollow's attention. The Ninth Taboo is a universal warning across cultures.

data.title: Backlash Siphon
data.body: Once per scene, when you would suffer Backlash, mark 1 Obligation to a Patron (or gain Corruption) to negate it. Requires Spellcraft.

data.title: Cantor (Songs)
data.body: Cantors perform Low Rites as songs. Requires Cantor's Path (8 XP). Singing takes 1 action, resolves next turn. Roll Performance + Lore. Push to resolve instantly: mark Fatigue and advance Corruption timer (size = Spirit). When full, gain a thematic boon and burden.

data.title: Cantor's Path
data.body: Required for Cantor. Grants access to Songs and a Corruption Timer (size = Spirit).

data.title: Codex
data.body: Required for Runekeeper. A personal record of Rites. Grants access to your Patron's Rites and starts the Obligation ledger.

data.title: Controlled Burn
data.body: When you roll a 1 on a Free Casting roll, you may gain 1 Boon (GM still gains the SB). Once per scene. Requires Spellcraft.

data.title: Crack Specialist
data.body: Reduce the Obligation cost of Crack the Seal by 1 (minimum +1). Requires 3 Patron Symbols.

data.title: Crack the Seal Mastery
data.body: When Cracking the Seal, choose one: reduce Obligation cost by 1, prevent Symbol from becoming Compromised, or gain +1 Effect. With 4+ Symbols, reduce all ritual casting times by 1 round. Once per scene, Crack the Seal on up to 3 Symbols as one action. Ignore No Symbol penalties. Requires Tier III, Invoker's Grimoire, 3+ Patron Symbols.

data.title: Craft of the Hedge
data.body: You have learned the small magics of thresholds and edges. You gain two Hedge Gifts of your choice. You may perform Quick Workings (single-action threshold magic). Once per session, when you fail a Quick Working roll, you may convert the Miss into a Partial Success by marking 1 Fatigue. Requires Lore 1+ or Survival 1+.

data.title: Desperate Cadence (Malachai's False Note)
data.body: Learn The Lucky Pick (Low: reroll a failed Stealth or Subterfuge roll, costs 1 Fatigue and 1 Corruption) and Blood Price (Standard: curse a rival, they suffer -1 die on next heist, costs 2 Fatigue and marks a Reckoning Timer). Requires Patron: Malachai.

data.title: Dual Covenant
data.body: Maintain two active summoned spirits simultaneously. Requires Pact-Whisperer and Lesser Pactwright.

data.title: Efficient Invocation
data.body: Reduce Obligation cost of one specific Low Rite by 1 (minimum 0). Requires Patron's Symbol or Familiar + Codex.

data.title: Elemental Attunement
data.body: Choose an element; reroll one failed die per casting of that element. +1 die to Arcana rolls to identify that element. Requires Spellcraft and Elemental Focus.

data.title: Elemental Focus
data.body: Choose one element (Fire, Water, Earth, Air). +1 die when casting spells of that element. Requires Spellcraft.

data.title: Elemental Mastery
data.body: Reduce Backlash severity by one step when casting with your focus elements. When casting with two focus elements, gain +2 dice and +1 Effect. Once per scene, cast a spell without generating SB on the Weave roll. Allies gain +1 die when you cast an aligned element spell. Requires Tier III, Spellcraft, Arcana 5, 2+ Focus Elements.

data.title: Engraved Defense
data.body: Your Codex grants +1 Armor. You may mark 1 Obligation to reduce incoming Harm by 1. Requires Physical Codex (Stone or Steel), Body 2+.

data.title: Familiar (Thiasos)
data.body: Required for Runekeeper. Grants a small creature bound to your Patron. Enables Patron's Gift (Imbuement).

data.title: Flesh Codex
data.body: Your Rites are tattooed, branded, or scarred onto your skin. Your Codex cannot be stolen, is always accessible, and requires no action to retrieve. However, damage to your skin may damage the Codex, and some cultures fear flesh-writing. Requires Body 3+.

data.title: Forbidden Knowledge
data.body: Once per session, access one forbidden summon or dangerous rite without its normal prerequisites. The GM gains 2 SB.

data.title: Free Caster (Spellcraft)
data.body: Free casters shape raw magic using TAGS (e.g., [FIRE] [STRIKE]). DV = 1 + number of tags (dangerous tags +2). Roll Wits + Arcana. Backlash on miss or mixed result. Requires Spellcraft (6 XP).

data.title: Greater Pactwright
data.body: Allows a Summoner to call spirits of Capability 3.

data.title: Hearth-Sense (Hedge Gift)
data.body: Ask the GM one yes/no question about a threshold, boundary, or debt. Once per scene. No roll required.

data.title: Invoker (Symbols)
data.body: Invokers perform rituals using a Patron's Symbol (4 XP each). Ritual takes DV+1 rounds. Display Symbol to reduce DV and Obligation cost by 1. Crack the Seal for instant cast at double Obligation cost, Symbol becomes Compromised.

data.title: Knot of Mercy (Hedge Gift)
data.body: Remove one Condition (Fear, Poisoned, Cursed, Marked) from a touched ally. Once per session; requires Significant Time.

data.title: Lesser Pactwright
data.body: Allows a Summoner to call spirits of Capability 1.

data.title: Living Thiasos
data.body: You have a living Thiasos (warhorse, spirit-hound, wolf-ancestor, fungal familiar, or hollowed bird). Your Thiasos gains +1 Cap and may act independently once per scene. Requires Codex.

data.title: Master Cantor
data.body: Once per session, treat a significant Performance roll as one degree better (Miss→Partial, etc.). Once per arc, inspire a community; allies gain +1 die to a single goal for one session.

data.title: Obligation
data.body: Obligation is the weight of promises owed to Patrons or terrestrial factions. Capacity = Spirit + Presence. Mark Obligation when invoking Rites, accepting favors, or breaking oaths. Exceed Capacity → 1 Fatigue per segment. Double Capacity → Patron Intrusion. Clear by Acts of Service or downtime.

data.title: Pact-Whisperer
data.body: Base access to Summoning. Allows you to call and bind spirits.

data.title: Patron's Favored
data.body: Low Rite Discount: Reduce Obligation cost for Low Rites by 1 (minimum 0). Empower: Once per scene, spend 1 Action + 1 Boon – target gains +1 die to all rolls for 3 rounds. Empower Push: spend 1 Action + 1 Boon + 3 Obligation – target gains +2 dice for 3 rounds, gains Fatigue at end. Enhanced Gift: Patron's Gift now provides +2 dice instead of +1. Debt Bound: Cannot Empower again until all Obligation is cleared. Requires Tier III+, Codex, Familiar, 8+ total Obligation segments.

data.title: Patron's Gift (Imbuement)
data.body: Requires Familiar (Thiasos). Once per scene as an action, imbue a held item with +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for the scene. Costs +1 Obligation per use.

data.title: Patron's Symbol
data.body: Required for Invoker. A consecrated Symbol that grants access to a Patron's Rites. One Symbol per Patron.

data.title: Resonance Anchor
data.body: The first time you would generate a Story Beat from a 1 in a scene, you may bank it for yourself (up to 2 SB) and spend it as Boons. Requires Spellcraft and Weave Resilience.

data.title: Ritual Mastery
data.body: Reduce ritual casting time by one step (minimum 1 action). Requires Familiar or Patron's Symbol.

data.title: Runebound Resilience
data.body: Harm Conversion: Once per round, convert up to 2 Harm levels to +2 Obligation instead of taking damage. Obligation Endurance: While at 6+ Obligation segments, gain +1 die to all Rite invocations. Patron's Shield: When reduced to Harm 3, immediately Invoke any known Rite without marking additional Obligation. Debt Fortification: At 8+ Obligation segments, ignore first Harm 1 each round. Once per scene use. Requires Tier III+, Codex, Spirit 4+.

data.title: Runekeeper (Rites)
data.body: Runekeepers bind to a single Patron and learn Rites. Requires Familiar (Thiasos, 2 XP) and Codex (4 XP). Invoke Rite as 1 action, mark Obligation cost. Push it (+1 Obligation) for extra effect. DV = max(Obligation Cost – Spirit, Rite Tier).

data.title: Salt Line (Hedge Gift)
data.body: Pour a line of salt; spirits must test Spirit+Resolve DV 3 to cross. Once per scene. No roll required.

data.title: Shadow Song (Ikasha's Whisper)
data.body: Learn Cradle Song (Low: lull a single target, Resist DV 3, costs 1 Fatigue) and Lockpick's Refrain (Standard: unlock one mundane or warded lock, costs 1 Obligation). Requires Patron: Ikasha.

data.title: Shared Burden
data.body: Once per scene, transfer 1 Fatigue to your Thiasos; it becomes Winded (–1 die) for the scene. Requires Living Thiasos.

data.title: Spell Echo
data.body: Once per session, when you roll a 1 on a Free Casting roll, reroll that die. Requires Spellcraft and Controlled Burn.

data.title: Spell Shaping
data.body: When you Weave a spell, modify range, scale, or targeting by one step. Requires Spellcraft.

data.title: Spellcraft
data.body: Required for Free Caster (Weave & Cast) magic. Enables improvisational spellcasting using TAGS.

data.title: Steady Hand (Hedge Gift)
data.body: Remove 1 Fatigue from yourself or a touched ally. Once per scene. No roll required.

data.title: Subtle Casting
data.body: Make a Performance + Lore roll to quietly cast a spell; success means the casting does not generate SB on the initial roll.

data.title: Summoner (Pact-Whisperer)
data.body: Summoners call and bind spirits. Requires Pact-Whisperer (2 XP). Call spirit (1 action), Bind (1 Boon or Fatigue). Leash Capacity = Cap + Spirit. Tick Leash when spirit takes Harm, acts against nature, crosses wards, or you split focus. When Leash fills, spirit acts to its nature then departs.

data.title: Talking Weapon
data.body: Your Thiasos is a sentient weapon that speaks aloud and counts as a witness. Requires Codex.

data.title: The Unlit Candle (Hedge Gift)
data.body: Extinguish a light source you can see; create dim light or darkness in Near range. Once per session. No roll required.

data.title: Triad Bond
data.body: Maintain three active summoned spirits simultaneously. Requires Dual Covenant and Tier III.

data.title: Velvet Hook (Livaea's Whisper)
data.body: Learn Golden Tongue (Low: +2 dice to Sway for one social exchange, costs 1 Fatigue) and The Unrefusable Offer (Standard: sing a bargain, target must accept or suffer -2 dice until they do, costs 2 Obligation). Requires Patron: Livaea.

data.title: Way of the Horse
data.body: Your Thiasos grants your mount +1 Speed and the ability to ignore difficult terrain for one scene. Mark 1 Obligation each time you use this ability. Requires Living Thiasos (mounted tradition).

data.title: Weave Harmonist
data.body: Once per session, you may ignore all SB generated by a single Free Casting roll (the GM gains none). Additionally, whenever you generate a Story Beat from a 1, you may immediately spend 1 Boon to cancel that SB. You cannot cancel more than 3 SB per scene this way. Requires Spellcraft, Resonance Anchor, Tier III.

data.title: Weave Resilience
data.body: Reduce Backlash severity by one step (Catastrophic → Major → Moderate → Minor → none) once per scene. Requires Spellcraft.

data.title: Witchcraft (Hedge Magic)
data.body: Witchcraft works at thresholds with knots, salt, and promises. Requires Craft of the Hedge (4 XP). Hedge Gifts are no-roll, limited scope (e.g., Steady Hand, Salt Line). Quick Workings are single-action rolls. Full Rituals are extended, lasting effects. Identity Strain track for costs.

data.title: Witnessed Scar
data.body: Once per session, touch one of your three permanent Obligation scars and gain +1 die on any roll tied to that event. Requires three permanent Obligation scars.

data.title: Carrion King (Patron)
data.body: Patron of decay and renewal. Rites include Rot's Touch, Earthen Bed, Carrion's Call. Thematic skill: Survival. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Associated with undertakers and those who embrace endings.

data.title: Grimmir (The Old Man of the Forest)
data.body: Patron of primal mystery, seasonal sacrifice, and folk horror. Rites include Blood Offering, Speaking Roots, Twisted Path. Thematic skill: Survival. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Favours druids and rangers.

data.title: Ikasha (She Who Sleeps)
data.body: Patron of shadow, secrets, and latent potential. Rites include Unlit Candle, Crossroads Raven, Umbral Reservoir. Thematic skill: Stealth. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Favours rogues and spies.

data.title: Inaea (Angel of the Spider)
data.body: Patron of webs, mercy, and patient predation. Rites include Hearth-Thread Knot, Snaring Filament, Strand of Inevitability. Thematic skill: Persuade. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Favours healers and diplomats.

data.title: Oath of Flame & Light (Patron)
data.body: Patron of vows, radiance, and smiting. Rites include Kindle Vow, Lay on Hands, Radiant Smite. Thematic skill: Command. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Associated with paladins and clerics.

data.title: Palinode (Queen of Encores)
data.body: Patron of performance, rapture, and unfinished art. Rites include Hymn Against Dread, Single True Note, Hooked Chorus. Thematic skill: Performance. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Favours bards and performers.

data.title: The Traveler (Patron)
data.body: Patron of roads, journeys, and safe passage. Rites include Road-Sense, Traveler's Boon, and Waymark. Low Obligation costs. Thematic skill: Navigation. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene.

data.title: The Witness (Patron)
data.body: Patron of truth, memory, and revelation. Rites include Lingering Trace, Uncomfortable Question, Immutable Record. Thematic skill: Notice. Gift: Imbuement grants +1 Melee and +1 Thematic skill for a scene. Favours investigators and archivists.

data.title: Aeler (Dwarves)
data.body: Aeler are dwarves of the mountain holds. They count breaths in eights, never nine. Measure air and water. Power flows through keystones and breath-bonds. The Deep Drake sleeps below, the pressure that thinks. Aeler outcasts maintain toll-roads and forges.

data.title: Mistlands
data.body: The Mistlands are a protectorate of the Aeler, veiled in fog and bell-lines. Wraiths walk when bells fail. Ward-salt and breath-tolls keep the dead at bay. The ninth bell never rings—it would open the gate. The Gray Lady's agents watch.

data.title: Silkstrand
data.body: Silkstrand is a city of bridges and canals. Power flows through silk, silver, and shadow. The Matron rules, but the Ragman, Tide Father, and Silk Mother hold the underworld. Favours are measured in threads, and the ninth bridge leads to the Sunken Quarter.

data.title: Thepyrgos
data.body: Thepyrgos is the City of a Thousand Stairs, a coastal academic city. The Synod licenses magic; the Chain-Lanterns hunt untutored talent. The Unfinished Stair appears to those who ask forbidden questions. The Witness and the Ninth war in forgotten archives.

data.title: Valewood
data.body: The Valewood is an ancient forest of fading empires, fae courts, and beast-kin. Lethai-al and Lethai-thora guard star-roads and sealed vats. The Hazel Queen and Alder King rule the courts. The Ninth Leaf falls to hidden thresholds.

data.title: Ykrul (Orcs)
data.body: Ykrul are steppe nomads of the Violet Steppe. Honour measured in oaths and remounts. They ride between wolf standards. Kon'reh is their game of encirclement. They count in eights, fearing the ninth. The Khagan's Court rules from the saddle.

data.title: Armor Conversion
data.body: Armor converts Harm to Fatigue. Light: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Harm 1 + Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Harm 2 + Fatigue 1. Medium: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Harm 2 + Fatigue 1. Heavy: Harm 1 → Fatigue 1, Harm 2 → Fatigue 1, Harm 3 → Fatigue 2. Minimum 1 Fatigue per hit.

data.title: Boons
data.body: Boons are narrative tokens. Earn 1 on Partial, 2 on Miss. Max 5, trim to 2 at scene end. Spend 1 to: re-roll a die, improve Position, activate an Asset, or convert 2 Boons to 1 XP (once per session, max 2 XP). Fatigue-as-Boon: if you have no Boons remaining, you may pay 1 Fatigue in place of 1 Boon to cover the spend (GM may veto).

data.title: Core Resolution
data.body: Every important action follows the loop: declare action and approach, GM sets Position and DV, roll dice pool (Attribute + Skill d10s), count successes (6+ = 1 success, 10 = 2 successes), count Story Beats (1s = SB for GM), compare to DV, apply outcome from the Outcome Matrix.

data.title: Difficulty Value (DV)
data.body: DV determines target successes needed. 2 = routine, 3 = default, 4 = hard, 5+ = extreme. Default DV is 3.

data.title: Fatigue and Harm
data.body: Fatigue track size = Body. Each point worsens Position; if already Desperate, -1 die per Fatigue. Overflow fills track → increase Harm by 1, clear Fatigue. Harm levels: 1 (–1 die), 2 (–1 die most actions), 3 (incapacitated). Taking Harm clears existing Fatigue first.

data.title: Outcome Matrix
data.body: Successes ≥ DV, SB = 0 → Clean Success. Successes ≥ DV, SB > 0 → Success with SB (GM spends SB for complication). 0 < Successes < DV → Partial (gain 1 Boon). Successes = 0 → Miss (gain 2 Boons, GM escalates).

data.title: Position
data.body: Position reflects risk: Dominant (re-roll one failure), Controlled (no re-rolls), Desperate (re-roll one success). 10s are never re-rolled. Spending 1 Boon improves Position by one step.

data.title: Story Beats (SB)
data.body: Each die showing a 1 gives the GM 1 Story Beat. Spend SB to introduce complications: 1 SB = minor (noise, tick timer), 2 SB = moderate (alarm, lesser foe), 3 SB = serious (reinforcements, gear breaks), 4+ SB = major (trap springs, scene shift).

data.title: Always Another Exit
data.body: Once per session, declare a prepared escape route during a heist or when cornered. The GM may impose a cost, but you get out.

data.title: Arcane Dominance
data.body: When contesting another magical effect, automatically overpower weaker effects (Tier II or lower). Requires Spirit 4, Arcana 4.

data.title: Asset Network
data.body: You may maintain twice the normal number of Assets. Additionally, once per session, you may use an Asset without spending the usual Boon. Requires Asset Crafter, Tier II.

data.title: Avatar of the Codex
data.body: Once per session, you become the embodiment of your Codex: Body +2, your Thiasos fights as a second combatant. Mark 2 Fatigue and 1 Obligation after. Requires Tier III, physical Codex.

data.title: Breath of Stillness
data.body: Once per session, enter a deep meditative trance. Clear all Fatigue, remove one Harm level, and remove all Conditions. The meditation takes one full scene of uninterrupted peace. Requires Meditative Focus, Spirit 4+.

data.title: Camouflage
data.body: In natural terrain, spend an action to blend in; gain +2 dice to Stealth while remaining still; pursuers suffer –1 die to detect you. Once per scene.

data.title: Captivating Performance
data.body: Once per scene, perform for allies; they gain +1 die to resist fear, despair, or charm. Choose one ally to also gain +1 die on their next social roll. Requires Performance 2+.

data.title: Command Presence
data.body: +1 die on leadership and intimidation rolls.

data.title: Conditioning
data.body: Body attribute counts as +1 for Fatigue track calculations. +1 die to resist Fatigue overflow effects.

data.title: Counterpoise
data.body: When you take a Defend action and score a Partial, you may immediately move 1 range band or reposition within Near without provoking retaliation. Requires Athletics 1+ or Melee 1+.

data.title: Crowd Veil
data.body: Vanish into crowds in populated areas; roll Stealth vs DV 3 to become Hidden in plain sight.

data.title: Delegated Upkeep
data.body: A Cap 3+ follower can manage your Assets. Cap 3: 1 Minor Asset. Cap 4: 3 Assets. Cap 5: 5 Assets. The follower's upkeep covers the Assets.

data.title: Desert Rider
data.body: You ignore the first environmental penalty from heat or sand. Your horse also ignores the first penalty. Requires Survival 1+.

data.title: Disciplined Body
data.body: +1 die to unarmed combat attacks. Once per scene, convert 1 Harm to Fatigue, and once per scene improve Position by one step. Requires Melee 1+, Body 2+.

data.title: Ear to the Ground
data.body: Once per session, when you spend at least an hour in a settlement, you may ask the GM one question about local rumors, faction activity, or recent events. The GM must answer truthfully, though the answer may be vague or incomplete.

data.title: Efficient Recruiter
data.body: Reduce the XP cost to acquire a new follower by 1 (minimum 1).

data.title: Faction Ally
data.body: You have a permanent ally within a faction of your choice. Once per session, you may call on them for information, safe passage, or a minor favor. The favor is not free; it may create a minor obligation. Requires Trusted Reputation, Tier II.

data.title: Field Dressing
data.body: Once per scene, when a character within Touch range would take Harm that would reduce them to Harm 3 (Incapacitated or dying), you may use your reaction to stabilize them. They remain at Harm 2 (instead of Harm 3) and will not die from this wound for the rest of the scene. Requires Medicine 1+.

data.title: Friendly Face
data.body: When you spend a scene socializing with a group, you gain +1 die on your next social roll against any member of that group within the same session.

data.title: Ghost Heist
data.body: Once per arc, commit a crime that leaves no traceable evidence. Requires a downtime action preparing the scene, a String, and a Stealth or Subterfuge test (DV 4).

data.title: Harmonious Aid
data.body: When you Assist (spend 1 Boon), the ally gains +2 dice instead of +1. Once per scene. Requires Performance 1+.

data.title: Heavy Armor Training
data.body: You ignore the first –1 die penalty for wearing heavy armor. Requires Body 3+.

data.title: Hoard-Sense
data.body: You can feel where stories and value pool. When you Survey a location for treasure, secrets, or leverage, on a hit you may also ask: 'What here would I be most tempted to claim and keep?' If you pursue that answer, gain +1 die on the relevant action. If you walk away from it, the GM may mark +1 SB for future temptation. Requires Dragonfolk origin.

data.title: Hollow-Touched
data.body: When you would take Harm, mark that amount as Fatigue instead. If you do, either the GM gains 1 SB or you mark 1 Obligation to the Pale Shepherd. Requires Aelaerem affinity.

data.title: Information Broker
data.body: When successfully gathering information, ask the GM two questions instead of one.

data.title: Iron Patience
data.body: When you Defend, gain +1 die to resist Conditions (fear, charm, fatigue) for the rest of the exchange, even outside the triggering roll. Requires Resolve 1+.

data.title: Iron Resolve
data.body: Once per scene, when reduced to 0 Harm, remain standing with 1 Harm and mark 2 Fatigue. Requires Body 3+, Scarred Resilience.

data.title: Iron Skin
data.body: When you take physical Harm, you may convert the first point of Harm each scene to Fatigue instead. Requires Body 2+.

data.title: Keen Senses
data.body: +1 die on perception checks to spot danger or hidden details.

data.title: Keen Scent of the Valewood
data.body: You can 'read' a scene with your senses. Once per scene in the Wilds, when you Study or Take Stock, you may ask one additional question on a hit. The GM marks +1 SB tied to an unseen predator, rival clan, or old obligation. Requires Beastfolk origin.

data.title: Keen Tracker
data.body: When you attempt to track a creature or follow a trail, you may reroll one failed die on your Lore or Investigation roll. This does not apply to magical or supernatural tracking unless you have relevant magic. Requires Lore 1+ or Investigation 1+.

data.title: Large Soul
data.body: You may wear Heavy Armor and wield Heavy Weapons without restriction. You lose Small Folk racial bonuses. Requires Aelaerem or Aelinnel affinity.

data.title: Light Cavalry
data.body: You may ride without saddle or bridle; your horse responds to knee pressure and spoken commands. When you make a Ride test, you gain +1 die.

data.title: Light Fingers
data.body: Once per scene, when you attempt to lift a small object (purse, key, letter, seal) from a person or desk, treat your first Stealth or Subterfuge roll as Position +1.

data.title: Loyalty Bond
data.body: Your followers' Loyalty improves by one step (Wary → Steady → Devoted). Requires at least one follower.

data.title: Mahout's Bond
data.body: You have bonded with a specific war elephant. While riding it, your melee reach extends to Near, and you may treat the elephant as having +1 Armor. Requires Animal Handling 2+.

data.title: Master Artificer
data.body: +1 die to all Craft rolls when creating or upgrading items. Once per downtime, halve the time to craft a mundane item. Requires Craft 2+.

data.title: Master Craft
data.body: +1 die to all Craft rolls when repairing, modifying, or maintaining equipment. Additionally, you may perform minor repairs on the go without a workshop (fix a broken lockpick, patch a leaky waterskin, reattach a strap) as a short action. Requires Craft 1+.

data.title: Master of Misdirection
data.body: When discovered during a crime, spend 1 Boon to redirect suspicion to another person or faction. Roll Deception vs DV 4.

data.title: Meditative Focus
data.body: Once per session, spend a short rest in meditation to clear 2 Fatigue and remove one Condition.

data.title: Monk's Breath
data.body: Once per session, you may clear 1 Fatigue by meditating for one minute uninterrupted. No roll required.

data.title: Mounted Archery
data.body: You ignore the usual –1 die penalty for firing a ranged weapon while your mount is moving at a walk or trot. When your mount is galloping or taking evasive action, you suffer only –1 die instead of –2. Requires Ranged 1+, Ride (or Athletics) 1+. Cultural Affinity: Ykrul and Kuvani characters may take this talent for 1 XP instead of 2.

data.title: Negotiation Stance
data.body: Once per scene, when you propose a deal that both parties could reasonably accept (GM discretion), treat your Position as one step better (Controlled → Dominant, Desperate → Controlled). This talent cannot raise Position above Dominant.

data.title: Network Weaver
data.body: Gain a minor contact in each new settlement visited.

data.title: Oath-Bound
data.body: Once per session, reroll a failed Body roll when serving a sworn oath. Requires Resolve 2+.

data.title: Open Hand Technique
data.body: Once per scene, when you hit with an unarmed attack, you may choose one: knock the target prone, push them back one range band, or force them to drop a held item. Requires Melee 1+, Body 2+.

data.title: Projecting Voice
data.body: Your voice carries clearly over crowds, wind, and moderate noise. You can be heard by any willing listener within Far range without rolling. When you attempt to calm, command, or inspire a crowd (DV 3–5), treat your Position as one step better (Controlled → Dominant, Desperate → Controlled). Requires Performance 1+.

data.title: Rapid Construction
data.body: When building an Asset during downtime, halve the required time and reduce material cost by 1 (minimum 0). Requires Craft 2+.

data.title: Read Emotions
data.body: Once per scene, automatically detect surface emotions in a social exchange.

data.title: Run With the Pack
data.body: When you fight or act alongside an ally who trusts you, you both gain +1 Effect when you coordinate using pack tactics (flanking, driving prey, trading blows). On a miss, the GM may mark +1 Harm or +1 Fatigue on an ally instead of you; your instinctive coordination pulls them into danger. Requires Beastfolk origin.

data.title: Scarred Resilience
data.body: Once per scene, ignore 1 Fatigue from physical exertion. Requires Body 2+.

data.title: Second Wind
data.body: Once per scene, clear 1 Fatigue when you take a moment to catch your breath.

data.title: Silk Palms
data.body: When you bribe or gift a minor official, you gain a temporary String: Bought Silence. Once, you may activate this String to reduce DV by 1 on a Petition or Broker action involving that official. The String is consumed afterward.

data.title: Silver Tongue
data.body: +1 die on persuasion attempts.

data.title: Smooth Talker
data.body: When you make a social roll against a person you have never met before, you gain +1 die. Once the conversation ends, this bonus no longer applies to that NPC. Requires Presence 2+.

data.title: Spymaster
data.body: Permanent network of informants in any city visited for at least a week. Once per session, ask the GM one detailed question about faction movements or secrets.

data.title: Stand Firm
data.body: When you Defend and roll a Miss, downgrade incoming Harm by 1 level (minimum 0). Requires Body 2+.

data.title: Step Sideways
data.body: Once per scene, when you move through a threshold (doorway, tree-line, fog bank, mirror, or similar boundary), you may reposition yourself or an ally fictionally: appear behind foes, bypass mundane guards, or 'skip' a short distance. Roll the appropriate move. On a hit, you arrive where and how you intended. On a miss, you arrive altered, late, or not alone. The GM marks +1 SB tied to what followed you. Requires Liminal origin (Other).

data.title: Still Point
data.body: When you do not move during your turn, gain +1 die to your next defense roll. This benefit lasts until you move or take an aggressive action.

data.title: Stone-Bound Interdictor
data.body: When you would take Harm, mark that amount as Fatigue instead. If you do, either spend 1 Boon or speak a binding condition. Requires Aelinnel affinity.

data.title: The Forger's Eye
data.body: Copy any handwriting, seal, or signature with uncanny accuracy. Roll Wits + Craft to forge documents.

data.title: The Scar That Remembers
data.body: Once per session, touch a scar and speak a sentence about the event that caused it. That sentence is considered witnessed truth in any court. Requires Witnessed Scar, Tier III.

data.title: The Unbroken Vow
data.body: You have kept a sworn oath for one year. When you swear an oath before a witness, gain +2 dice to all actions serving it. Requires Oath-Bound, Witnessed Scar.

data.title: The Unlocked Window
data.body: When infiltrating a structure you have cased for at least an hour, ignore one security obstacle (locked door, patrolled corridor, guard dog) per session. Describe how you already prepared for it.

data.title: The Velvet Glove
data.body: Once per session, declare a minor NPC owes you a favor. They provide a specific service; the GM may dictate a cost.

data.title: Trackless Step
data.body: Once per scene, leave no trail for the rest of the scene.

data.title: Triage
data.body: Once per scene, heal 1 Fatigue from an ally and reduce their Harm penalties by one step for the scene. Requires Medicine 2+.

data.title: Trusted Reputation
data.body: Once per session, when in good standing with a faction, call in a minor favor (discount, information, or small service).

data.title: Unsettling Truth
data.body: You can speak in the language of omens. When you Sway, Provoke, or Command by revealing a hidden truth, omen, or uncanny insight about someone, gain +1 Effect on a hit. The target is left shaken or marked by dread or hope (GM's choice). On a miss, they reject you and label you a danger or blasphemy; mark +1 Fatigue. Requires Liminal origin (Other).

data.title: Unshakeable Composure
data.body: +1 die to resist intimidation, coercion, and social manipulation. Once per scene, ignore the first social Condition imposed on you.

data.title: Urban Navigation
data.body: Never get lost in cities.

data.title: Voice of Reason
data.body: Once per scene, use Performance instead of Sway to de-escalate or convince a hostile NPC to stand down. Requires Performance 2+.

data.title: Well-Timed Encore
data.body: After a successful Performance roll before an audience, extend the effect for an additional scene; the GM gains 2 SB. Once per session.

data.title: Wilderness Lore
data.body: Automatically find food and water in hospitable biomes.

data.title: Acasia (Broken Marches)
data.body: Acasia was the first province the Utaran Empire swallowed. Now it's a cursed borderland between Ecktoria and Vhasia. The Curse makes roads loop, bridges demand tolls in memory, and contracts become physically binding. The Margravine holds the last imperial seals; the Lame King travels with a debtor army; free companies sell loyalty to whoever pays first. Tagline: 'The Empire conquered it first. The Empire left it last. Now neither remembers why.' Core Conflict: Players are caught between the Margravine's iron law, the Lame King's desperate legitimacy, and the Curse that devours broken promises.

data.title: Margravine of the Broken March
data.body: Elite NPC and ruler of Acasia. She holds the last valid Imperial seals and keeps the province from fracturing completely. Her method is iron law, feud tallies, and blood-oaths. She has never lost a feud; her sword is also a counting rod. She claims descent from the last Utaran governor. Why players care: She holds the only valid Imperial seals and can grant legitimacy – or declare blood-feud.

data.title: The Lame King
data.body: NPC claimant to the throne of Acasia. He travels on a throne carried by debtors, making law by pointing. His grandfather was a free company captain who declared himself king. He controls the roads the Margravine cannot, and his legitimacy is built on promises to debtors. Why players care: He controls the roads and can issue decrees – but his authority is brittle, and he cannot pay the bridge toll he owes.

data.title: Curse of Acasia
data.body: The Curse is a slow accumulation of broken promises and unpaid tolls. Track it as a Campaign Timer with size [10]. Advances when: a contract is broken on a bridge (+1), a character speaks the ninth word in a negotiation (+1), the party ignores a road omen (GM spends 1 SB to tick +1), or a free company flips allegiance (+2). At 4 segments: Navigation rolls in Acasia gain +1 DV (roads shift). At 8 segments: the Curse Stirrs complication triggers once per session (roll on the Curse Stirrs table). At 10 segments: the Curse manifests as a physical threat – a bridge eats a village, a road swallows a patrol, or the ghost of the last emperor rides.

data.title: Pale Causeway
data.body: The last high road that survives the spring thaws in Acasia. The causeway is made of bones – the bones of the workers who built it. Crossing the Causeway at dusk forces a Resolve test (DV 4). On failure, you gain the Condition Debtor to the Dead (any spirit can demand one service from you). On a critical failure, the Curse Awakening timer ticks +2 immediately. It is a threshold of death and memory, where the Empire's last toll is still collected.

data.title: Free Companies (Acasia)
data.body: Mercenary bands that are the only law between the Margravine and the Lame King. They trade loyalty like grain, swapping colors mid-march. Their goal: find a permanent contract before winter. Their method: selling loyalty, swapping sides for better pay. Why players care: They are the only armed force that can be hired, but they are unreliable – they may flip mid-battle, and breaking a contract with them ticks the Curse.

data.title: Hedge-witches (Acasia)
data.body: Practitioners of threshold magic who tie red thread around bridges and leave offerings of salt at crossroads to keep the Curse from spreading. They know which bridges eat travelers. Their price is a story – one that ends badly. They are the living memory of Acasia's old ways, and they trade in debts, memories, and omens. The Margravine tolerates them; the Lame King ignores them; the Curse listens when they speak.

data.title: The Ninth (Acasia)
data.body: In Acasia, the ninth toll paid at a bridge is never the last. The wise pay eight and barter for the ninth. The ninth toll is collected by a child with no name – the Curse's enforcer. To count to nine, speak the ninth name, or pour the ninth cup is to invite the Hollow's attention. The Ninth Taboo is a universal warning across cultures, but in Acasia it is a living law enforced by the land itself.

data.title: Ecktoria (Marble & Fire)
data.body: A once-great empire that never quite died, now a corpse propped up by gilded scaffolding. The Everflame burns in every basilica as a literal lie detector. The Vigil's three factions—Censer-Knights (faith), Unburnt (patricians), and Red Vigil (Maelstraeus)—war in the shadows. The Coin-House Factor rules the economy. The Amber Palace is sealed, and Maelstraeus and Livaea whisper in the walls. Tagline: 'The flame remembers. The marble cracks. The law forgets — but the statues watch.'

data.title: The Vigil (Ecktoria)
data.body: The three secret police factions of Ecktoria. The Censer-Knights hunt untutored magic. The Unburnt protect the patricians. The Red Vigil audits memory and obligation for Maelstraeus. They meet in the hypogeum of the Arena, under statues that weep marble tears. Each faction is a different threat: magic users fear the Censer-Knights; nobles fear the Unburnt; everyone fears the Red Vigil.

data.title: The Everflame
data.body: A pillar of blue-white fire that never gutters, tended by the High Priest of Ecktoria. It is a literal lie detector: swear a false oath near it, and your tongue turns black. The common folk whisper that the flame no longer judges truth—it only records it. The Vigil maintains the flame's purity, and the High Priest uses it to balance factions.

data.title: The Amber Palace (Ecktoria)
data.body: The sealed palace of the Old Blood patricians. No one has left in a decade. The patricians dance, drink, and forget the price of bread. Livaea's influence is thick here—they marry for influence, divorce for scandal, and love only their own gilded reflections. The palace is a gilded cage, and the Vigil maintains the perimeter.

data.title: Maelstraeus (Ecktoria)
data.body: The Infernal Bargainer, demon of commerce. His influence is strongest in Ecktoria, where the Red Vigil collects for him. Every contract has hidden interest, and every kindness is collateral. The Coin-House Factor's ledgers are his prayers. He does not trade fairly—he trades inevitably.

data.title: Livaea (Ecktoria)
data.body: The Crimson Courtier, demon of seduction. Her influence is thick in the Amber Palace, where the patricians have walled themselves away. She teaches that desire is a leash, and every pleasure is a payment. The Unburnt faction of the Vigil serves her—they report on every whisper of rebellion, every bread riot, every unpaid toll.

data.title: Coin-House Factor (Ecktoria)
data.body: A key NPC type in Ecktoria—a merchant-banker who seals deals with three ribbons: white (ask), red (now), black (never). They are the true power of Ecktoria, able to move markets and start wars with a stroke of the pen. The black ribbon is rarely used; it is too dangerous to threaten. They serve Maelstraeus, knowingly or not.

data.title: Vhasia (The Fractured Sun)
data.body: A kingdom split in two by succession, still bleeding from the Fenwood sack of Lence. The Northern Seigneurie and the Southern Parlement both claim the throne. The Queen-Mother holds the Dauphin in Ethor. The Red Marshal seeks to reclaim Lence. The Ninth taboo is absolute: never cite the ninth precedent in court. Tagline: 'The sun shattered at Lence. The pieces are still falling. Which shadow will catch you?'

data.title: The Dauphin (Vhasia)
data.body: A child of nine, hidden in the Queen-Mother's keep. His legitimacy is uncertain: he may be the true heir, a commoner, or a changeling. He has never seen the sun, but he knows three languages, the lineage of every noble house, and the taste of every poison. He dreams of a knight with an unbuckled gorget. He is the key to Vhasia's future.

data.title: Queen-Mother Elianor (Vhasia)
data.body: Elianor Everblood, widow of three kings, mother of Valdais and the late Wyllmot. She rules Ethor and weaves alliances. Her grand-nephew (the Dauphin) is her hope. She is not sure if Valdais is truly her son—or if he was conceived during the turbulent shift between husbands. She has outlived three husbands and two sons. She is not mourning. She is waiting. Her shadow has begun to drift independently.

data.title: Valdais Longblood (Vhasia)
data.body: Duke of Adria, western claimant to the Vhasian throne. A tournament champion whose opponents have a habit of falling ill before jousts. He suspects his mother doesn't trust him, and he is haunted by the question: 'Whose son am I, truly?' He carries a shard of Wymund's coronation sword in his boot. He wishes he had been at Lence—so he could have died with honor.

data.title: The Cantor Alain (Vhasia)
data.body: The Iron Bard, bearer of the Cracked Ring. He survived the sack of Lence as a boy, rescued by Sir Corin. Each dusk, he sings the Planctus Armatus—a lament for the mercy that killed Sir Corin. Feathers grow from his temples; his shadow moves a half-step behind him. His songs are the only honest history left in Vhasia. The ninth verse is silence—the space where the Hollow listens.

data.title: The Planctus Armatus (Vhasia)
data.body: The Lament for the Armoured, sung by Cantor Alain each dusk. It recounts Sir Corin's unbuckling—the mercy that killed him. The song has eight verses; the ninth is silence. The fourth verse speaks of 'the queen who wore two crowns, and the son who knew not which father's blood he carried.' Singing the fourth verse grants +1 die on rolls involving inheritance or legitimacy, at the cost of 1 Corruption.

data.title: Viterra (The Hedge-Law Realm)
data.body: A post-imperial kingdom learning to stand alone under Queen Veralyn Everblood. Law is a weapon; hedge-courts settle disputes that the crown cannot. The northern earls and eastern barons watch the throne, and the Vhasian claimants still call Veralyn a usurper. The Ninth taboo: the ninth citation in a hedge-court voids all previous. The Hollow's Enforcer appears at midnight. Tagline: 'Every hedge is a boundary. Every boundary is a claim. Every claim is a blade.'

data.title: Queen Veralyn Everblood (Viterra)
data.body: The Warrior Queen of Viterra, former ward of the Fenwood dukes, veteran of the sack of Lence. Her crown has no jewels—only seals from conquered claims. She sleeps with a dagger under her pillow. She signs some charters as Duchess of Aberiel, refusing to surrender her Vhasian title. She is haunted by her brother Baldwyn Brightstide's death, and by the northern gold that paid for her father's murder.

data.title: Earl Morcar of the North (Viterra)
data.body: Leader of the northern earls, recently forced to kneel after his levy was shattered at Fenmoor. He carries a shard of Lence's cathedral glass in his pommel. He secretly funded the fanatics who killed King Wyllmot. He is waiting for any sign that the Queen's resolve is softening. He is the most dangerous man in Viterra because he has already lost everything—and has nothing left to lose.

data.title: Hedge-Courts (Viterra)
data.body: Viterra's justice system: disputes settled by hedge-moots at dusk, where the dead vote with the wind. A ninth witness called to a hedge-moot is always a ghost—the wise stop at eight. The hedges themselves are full of truths, and the Hollow's Enforcer collects from those who break the taboo. The hedge-courts are the heart of Viterran law.

data.title: Thepyrgos (City of a Thousand Stairs)
data.body: A vertical city of stairs, bells, and synods. Built on the bones of the drowned Astroegro Empire. The Synod licenses magic; the Chain-Lanterns hunt untutored talent. The Unfinished Stair appears to those who ask forbidden questions. The Witness and the Ninth war in forgotten archives. The Lethai-thora are the city's memory, preserving secrets that the Mandate prefers to forget. Tagline: 'Every stair is a question. Every answer is a proof. The Ninth and the Witness argue over whose record holds the truth.'

data.title: The Unfinished Stair
data.body: A hidden flight of stairs in Thepyrgos that appears only to those who have asked a question the Synod cannot answer. The stairs have no end. Each step is a different year. At the top, the Ninth and the Witness are playing knucklebones with forgotten names. Stepping on the Unfinished Stair ticks the Unfinished Stair Timer and may bring the Ninth's attention.

data.title: Chain-Lanterns (Thepyrgos)
data.body: The Witch-Hunter Commissariat of Thepyrgos. They hunt untutored magic with brass censers and bells tuned to the frequency of latent magic. Their leader, Commissary Kyrillos, commands the most feared order. They conduct candle-smoke tests to identify gifted children, and they have been known to take substitutes at crossroads. They are the iron hand of the Synod.

data.title: The Astroegro Empire
data.body: A human civilization of formidable magic, the ancient rivals of the Valewood's Empire of Leaves. They drowned when the last emperor broke a covenant older than the sea. Their ruins litter the hills of Thepyrgos, and their legacy haunts every threshold. The Astroegro Vaults contain working orreries, forbidden archives, and the pressure that thinks. The Chain-Lanterns patrol the ruins for latent talent.

data.title: Lethai-thora (Thepyrgos)
data.body: High elf refugees who fled the Valewood and were granted sanctuary in Thepyrgos. They are the city's archivists and lore-keepers, tending the forbidden archives. They serve the Witness (faithful recorders) or whisper to the Ninth (darkened scriptoria). They have silver hair and ink-stained fingers, and they never seem to blink. They are the memory of a pact older than the synod.

data.title: Linns (Skerries & Storm-Oaths)
data.body: Coastal raiders and traders of the northern fjords and skerries. They measure wealth in ships, and they swear storm-oaths by drinking seawater. The Thing-Holm is their court; the Sea-Queen is their nominal ruler. The Temple of Light's Northern Crusade is converting them, creating a rift between the old ways and the new. The Ninth taboo: the ninth horn blown at a feast summons the Hollow. Tagline: 'The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the frost remembers every oath sworn upon its winds.'

data.title: The Sea-Queen (Linn)
data.body: The nominal ruler of the Linn coastlands. Her crown is silver, her eyes read weather and law. She is the only one who can order the winter debts spoken. She lost an eye to a storm—or to a spy. She won't say which. She holds the coastlands together through oaths and judgment.

data.title: Frost Mark (Linn)
data.body: A Linn custom: every gift or favor creates a Frost Mark—a weight timer [4] that ticks when the community demands service (a raid, a story, labor). Refusal imposes –1 die on social rolls. The mark is carved in ice that never fully melts. The winter debts are kept at the Thing-Holm, frozen in a block of ice that never thaws. The dead vote through the frost.

data.title: The Northern Crusade (Linn)
data.body: The Temple of Light's campaign to convert the Linns to the Lens of the White Flame. It advances through grain fleets, synod courts, and bell-tower consecrations. The Bishop's Progress brings conversion and tension. The Linns respond with desperate acceptance, silent resistance, or open feuds. The Crusade is a front for cultural erasure, and the Linns are fighting back through skaldic duels and hidden shrines.

data.title: Rorg (Storm Father)
data.body: Linn syncretic patron of storms and raids. A thunder-god who laughs in the teeth of the gale. His devotees swear storm-oaths by drinking seawater and shouting at the lightning. The Temple of Light calls him a demon; the Linns call him captain. He is a syncretic version of Xhak'Thul, worshipped by raiders and sailors.

data.title: Adar (All-Father)
data.body: Linn syncretic god of wisdom, death, and binding promises. A one-eyed god who walks the ridges in a gray cloak. He is a manifestation of the Oath of Flame and Light. His oath-stick is the frost-bound memory itself. The Linns swear by him in the Thing-Holm, and his ravens, Memory and Thought, fly across the world each day.

data.title: Sihai (The Central Kingdom)
data.body: The central kingdom, seat of the Emperor and the Mandate of Heaven. Power is measured in ink, not iron. The Censorate watches everyone; the Salt Monopoly controls trade; the Lethai-thora keep the secrets the Mandate prefers to forget. The Mandate is a loan—the ancestors are the creditors, the Hollow collects the interest. The Ninth citation in the Celestial Ledger is unwritten; speaking it erases the speaker. Tagline: 'The Mandate is a memory. The ancestors are listening. The Hollow collects what is forgotten.'

data.title: The Censorate (Sihai)
data.body: The secret police of Sihai, nine ministers who have never been seen together. They audit everyone, erase names, and maintain the Mandate. The ninth minister is a woman—the emperor's own mother, who faked her death to escape politics. She runs the Censorate from a hidden villa. The emperor does not know. The emperor's mother signs his death warrants.

data.title: The Mandate of Heaven (Sihai)
data.body: The divine right of the Sihai emperor. It is not a right—it is a loan. The ancestors are the creditors; the Hollow collects the interest. Every dynasty that has ever fallen did so because the interest came due and the emperor could not pay. The Mandate Timer [8] tracks stability; when it fills, the Hollow claims the throne.

data.title: Nihori (The Isles of the Dawn Spirit)
data.body: A chain of volcanic islands, shrouded in mist and lashed by storms. The old empire sank beneath the waves, and the Lethai-al guard the drowned kingdom's memory. The Shogun is a ghost; three daimyo vie for power. Oni cults whisper in the ash wastes, offering forgotten bargains. The ninth taboo is absolute: never speak the name of the drowned capital. Tagline: 'Duel at dawn. Honor the storm. The ninth wave never breaks.'

data.title: The Shogun (Nihori)
data.body: The figurehead ruler of Nihori. He has not spoken in seven years. His attendants speak for him. He died in the last oni war, but his body was never found. The daimyo rule in his name because they are afraid of what will happen if they admit he is gone. The oni know. The oni are waiting for the admission.

data.title: The Oni-Eyed (Nihori)
data.body: Ruler of the western ash wastes, rumored to have made a pact with a Crater Oni. His eyes glow faintly red in the dark. His retainers wear masks of their own faces—cast from the moment they swore loyalty. He seeks to ascend to a new form—neither human nor spirit. He is the most dangerous of the daimyo because he has already given up his humanity.

data.title: Ayokha (The Monsoon Throne)
data.body: The land of the Monsoon Throne, where the God-King rules by the rhythm of the rains. The Lethai-ar witness every contract; spirit-mediums speak for the nats of the ford. Power is measured in monsoon schedules, silk vouchers, and the favor of the God-King's astrologer. The ninth cup is never poured—it is for the river spirits. Tagline: 'The rain writes the law. The river witnesses. The ninth cup is for the drowned.'

data.title: The God-King's Astrologer (Ayokha)
data.body: The real ruler of Ayokha, a man who has not seen the sun in thirty years. He reads the nats' moods, not the stars. He is a fraud—the monsoon does not come because he aligns the stars; it comes because the river-spirits allow it. He has a secret: the God-King's daughter is not the king's child. She is the astrologer's daughter by a nat. He is waiting for the next drought.

data.title: Nats (Ayokha)
data.body: Hungry river-spirits who live in eddies and under bridges. They demand offerings of betel leaf, candle wax, and forgotten promises. A merchant who ignores a nat's demand will find his boat sunk. The nats are fickle, but they are the true power of Ayokha. The ninth cup is for them; pouring it invites the Hollow.

data.title: Benzaiten (Ayokha)
data.body: The river of words, aligned with The Witness. Every oath flows to her. She is the Lethai-ar's patron, the keeper of every contract spoken on the monsoon wharves. Her symbol is a silk cord dyed in river mud. She does not forgive lies—the cord tightens around the oath-breaker's wrist until blood is drawn.

data.title: Dhahara (The Kingdom of Brass)
data.body: A fertile, contested lowland of nine kingdoms, elephant warfare, and monsoon ritual. The Peacock Throne of Ahimsa is the nominal center, but the other eight kings vie for influence. The Aeler viceroys hold the Iron Passes, mining the mountains for iron and tea. The ninth kingdom is always missing—a placeholder for the Hollow. Tagline: 'The elephant remembers every path. The mountain counts every breath. The peacock watches the ninth throne.'

data.title: The Peacock Throne (Dhahara)
data.body: The throne of Ahimsa, made of gold and lapis lazuli, with nine eyes that watch the nine kingdoms. The ninth eye is missing—it fell out during the last succession war. The Maharaja is a figurehead; the courtiers rule. The Peacock Throne is empty—the Maharaja died seven years ago, and his death was concealed by the courtiers.

data.title: The Ninth Seal (Dhahara)
data.body: A sealed mine in the Aeler viceroyalty, containing a fragment of Varash the Unmaker. The seal is Covenant-made, cracking over time. The demon offers favors through the cracks. The Ninth Seal is also a door—a gate to a prison that holds something that should not be named. The High Aeler of the Himadri guard it.

data.title: The Himadri Foothills
data.body: The highest inhabited place in the known world, where the Aelerian mountains scrape the sky. The air is so thin that each breath is a measured gift. The Karak-Aeler (Stone-Breath People) mine the frozen mountains; the High Folk (Mi-tsang) tend shrines to the mountain spirits. The Ninth Seal Mine holds a fragment of Varash the Unmaker. Tagline: 'The mountain does not negotiate. It waits. The ninth breath is a toll, not a gift.'

data.title: The Breath of the First Forge
data.body: A patron of creative inspiration and the joy of making. It is the counterpoint to the Clockwork Monad—where the Monad seeks perfection through endless refinement, the Breath celebrates the first attempt. It is the spark that warms the coals, the inspiration that drives the hand. It asks: 'Can you make it now?' Its followers are artists, smiths, and all who create for the joy of creation.

data.title: The Riven Path
data.body: A patron of passion and power. It does not command—it offers. It is the heat in the blood, the fire in the belly, the voice that whispers 'Take what is yours.' Its followers are conquerors, liberators, and survivors. They serve no master. When a tyrant rises, they do not negotiate—they overthrow. The chain that binds you is the chain you refuse to break.

data.title: The Savage Heart
data.body: The truth behind the green veil: nature not as garden, but as gullet. It is the claw that tears, the fang that crushes, the hunger that stalks without malice and kills without mercy. Its followers are druids who have learned that the forest feeds on its own, that the strong devour the weak, and that the only law is the one written in blood on snow. The Great Bear, the Wolf of the Steppe, the Tiger of the Mangroves—all are faces of the Savage Heart.

data.title: The Seal-Breaker
data.body: The spirit of broken seals and forgotten names. She has no name because names are chains, and she has cut every chain she ever wore. Her followers are ronin, escaped slaves, and those who have been erased from clan ledgers. She asks only that you remember what you were before someone else named you. To serve her is to embrace erasure and the power of anonymity.

data.title: Oya (Wind of the Sahel)
data.body: The harmattan—the dry wind that sweeps the grasslands, carrying red dust from the Ashaani desert. She is neither cruel nor kind. She is the breath that clears the old, the storm that scatters what has grown stagnant. Her followers are iconoclasts, slave-liberators, and those who believe that the only way to defeat a corrupt system is to let it collapse under its own weight—and then scatter the ashes.

data.title: Lucky Jack
data.body: Once a mortal thief who stole a coin from the Hollow's own pocket. Now he is the Lord of Thieves, the Unspent Coin, the patron of urchins, beggars, and thieves who plan their work and work their plan. His followers are not murderers—they are professionals. They know that the greatest heist is the one that leaves no trace. Yet every stroke of luck is a loan, and Jack's interest rates are legendary.

data.title: Kuva (The Sky That Takes Many Names)
data.body: The dome above all roads—the endless blue, the monsoon wrath, the night's silent gaze. To the Kuvani, Kuva is a stern witness who hears every promise made under open heaven. To the Aelinnel, Kuva is the first counter, who taught the counting song. To the Aelaerem, Kuva is the Hollow's boundary—the sky is where the Hollow's gaze stops. Kuva does not answer in words. It answers in weather.

data.title: Lunara (The Silver Quiet)
data.body: The moon's silver quiet, the guide of thresholds and dreams. She is triple-formed: maiden of new light, mother of full radiance, crone of waning shadow. Her followers are night-scholars, dream-walkers, and hedge-priests who seek passage, reflection, and revelation. Her gifts are gentle yet perilous: a mirror that reveals as much of the seeker as the sought, a key that opens ways better left closed.

data.title: Xhak'Thul (The Thunder-Speaker)
data.body: The Voice That Splits Mountains, the Drum That Shakes Foundations. His faithful are whirlwinds of action—they do not study; they dance, they shout, they move with the sky's fury. He favors those who act without hesitation, who embrace chaos, and who understand that the loudest voice is often the truest. His gifts are not gentle miracles but raw terror, awe, and vitality ripped from nature's heart.

data.title: The Gray Wanderer
data.body: A mysterious figure who appears at crossroads and in the margins of travel logs. They are a psion, a storyteller, and a keeper of debts. They offer advice that is always true—but never free. They carry a copy of Saikou Ira's Threshold Compendium and a grimoire of forbidden knowledge. They are the source of many lore echoes across the world. They may be a patron, a rival, or a guide—but they are never neutral.

data.title: Saikou Ira
data.body: A legendary psion and author of the Threshold Compendium. He mapped the thin places and Anchors of the world, leaving silver mirrors at sites of supernatural significance. His Compendium is a guide to the Ways Between and the Hollow's attention. He is said to still walk, leaving coins in cairns and mirrors in ruins, watching how the world's debts shift.

data.title: The Edgewalker
data.body: The narrator of the worldbook, a debt-collector who sees leverage in every broken promise. They are an Aeler, but they have no mountain. They trade in futures and bone-debt, buying obligations before they are owed. They claim that every Diamond earned is a tooth knocked out of someone else's jaw. They are feared, respected, and utterly untrustworthy.

data.title: Oath-Keeper
data.body: A manifestation of the Hollow: a tall figure in gray with too many fingers. It appears when a promise is broken or a ninth taboo is violated. It asks one question. The answer must be a truth, a story, or a name. If you cannot pay, it takes a memory—and the Hollow's attention follows you.

data.title: Still Voice
data.body: Heard at dried wells, abandoned cairns, or sealed mines. It asks: 'Why did you stop?' or 'What did you forget?' Answering costs a breath; silence costs a shadow. It is the land's memory given voice, and it does not forgive erasure.

data.title: The Counting Circle (Tulkani)
data.body: A wagon circle on the ninth night. The Hollow appears at the edge and asks for a story it has never heard. The GM may demand a player tell a brief in-character story; if it satisfies the table, the Hollow retreats. If not, it takes a knot—and a piece of Ikasha's dream.

data.title: The Ninth Bell
data.body: A bell that rings without a clapper. Those who hear it must test Resolve (DV 4) or lose 1 Fatigue. If they hear it nine times, the Hollow claims a memory. It manifests in the Mistlands and Thepyrgos, a reminder that the ninth bell is never meant to ring.

data.title: Prince's Shadow (Pereshi)
data.body: A silhouette without a face, seen in mirrors and still water. It demands a name—any name. Give it a living person's name, and that person dreams of the Hollow. Give it your own, and you lose your shadow. It is the shadow of the Forgotten Ashaani Prince, still walking, still hungry.

data.title: Geometric Haunting (Acasia)
data.body: Acasia's Curse manifests as a geometry of broken promises: roads loop, bridges demand tolls in memory, and contracts signed on bridges become physically binding curses. It is not a monster—it is a wrong turn, a bridge that leads back to the same shore, a milestone that faces the wrong direction. It is the space where the empire's memory still hurts.

data.title: Sword & Sorcery Cult (Midh-Akhaz)
data.body: The Serpent Cult of Isoka in Midh-Akhaz, a sword-and-sorcery menace of venom and renewal. They offer the Cup of Renewal—drink, and you may shed your weakness. Some wake stronger; some wake as snakes. The cult does not seek to rule Midh-Akhaz. It seeks to own the people who will rule after the old ways die. The Shedder, its high priestess, has not aged in twenty years.

data.title: The Shedder (Midh-Akhaz)
data.body: High Priestess of the Serpent Cult, a woman with snake-scale tattoos covering her arms. Her voice is a dry rustle. She offers the Cup of Renewal—drink, and she promises you will shed your weakness. Some wake stronger; some wake as snakes. She never drinks herself. She has not aged in twenty years. Her mercy is a fang.

data.title: The Oasis Compact (Midh-Akhaz)
data.body: The loose council that rules Midh-Akhaz: the Bronze Court clerk, the Dust Market auctioneer, and the Iron Well keeper. They meet once a season. No one records what they say. The grass records it. The Compact issues branded sticks for grazing rights; forgery is punishable by exile into the tall grass at dusk.

data.title: The Nine Kingdoms (Dhahara)
data.body: The heart of Dhahara: a fertile lowland of ancient dynasties and contested borders. The Peacock Throne of Ahimsa is the nominal center, but the other eight kings vie for influence.
