The number 'nine' is a ritual—a prayer that the Hollow will not notice that one of the nine is always missing. The missing kingdom is always the one that mattered.

data.title: The Iron Passes (Dhahara)
data.body: The high mountain passes of Dhahara, where the Aeler viceroys rule on behalf of the distant High King. The air is thin and cold; the passes are measured in breath-counts. Iron mines scar the hillsides, worked by Dhaharan laborers and overseen by Aeler engineers. The Ninth Seal Mine holds a fragment of Varash the Unmaker.

data.title: The Brass Coast (Dhahara)
data.body: Dhahara's southern rim: a humid, feverish coastline of palm groves, salt pans, and crowded port cities. Three powers bleed into each other here: the Kahfagian Admiralty (tolls), the Sidhi diaspora (ropeways, lighthouse courts), and the native Dhaharan rajas (land, pepper, iron). The ninth rope on every ropeway is frayed—a reminder of the dead who still pull their weight. Tagline: 'Three powers, one coast, and a memory written in salt.'

data.title: The Sidhi Diaspora
data.body: Refugees from Galanina who fled Ashaani slavers. They now run the ropeways, the lighthouse courts, and the freedman's seal on the Brass Coast. They are welcome nowhere and trusted less, but without them the spice trade stops. Their story is one of forced migration, memory, and survival. They keep green lamps lit for the dead.

data.title: The Ragman (Silkstrand)
data.body: The Lord of Unspoken Pacts, the crime lord who controls the Ropewalk and the Burdened Arcade. He collects broken promises in flesh, not silver. He is a patron of the Ninth, and his favor is the ninth thread—the one that is never cut. He is patient, polite, and utterly without mercy. He owns the bridges that lead to the Sunken Quarter.

data.title: The Tide Father (Silkstrand)
data.body: The crime lord who controls the flood-stairs and the night-boats. His divers recover what the canals hide. He is a patron of Khemesh, the Abyssal Maw, and his voice sounds like water filling a locked room. He owns the ninth step on every flood-stair—the one that is always underwater.

data.title: The Matron (Silkstrand)
data.body: The ruler of Silkstrand, a woman of velvet and iron. She has never raised her voice; the city learned to fear her silences. Her cord has nine knots—one for each family bound to her by old pacts. The ninth knot is loose, waiting for the one who will betray her. She is the balance between the patricians and the underworld.

data.title: Obligation as Currency
data.body: Across Fate's Edge, obligation is the true currency. Coins are a convenience; resources are a burden; power is a promise you have not yet been asked to keep. Every gift is a chain, every favor a thread, every promise a loan. The Hollow collects the interest. Track obligation with visible timers and story beats—it is the weight that moves the world.

data.title: The Clockwork Monad's Apocalypse
data.body: The Clockwork Monad is not merely a patron of craft—it is also an apocalyptic force. When civilization's technology reaches a critical threshold, the Monad stirs. Its pressure shifts from suggestion to command. It begins to optimize not only tools but flesh, not only craft but law. In the end, the Monad would leave a world of perfect, silent, interlocking efficiency: a clockwork Eden with no room for error, or for life.

data.title: The Unfired Crown (Pereshi)
data.body: The Pereshi do not kneel to a king. They kneel to fire, to ash, and to a name they erased. Each valley or fire-shrine city governs itself through a council of elders, a Flame-Keeper, and a war captain. There is no central treasury, no standing army, no code of laws beyond custom and the witness of the ninth coal. Their unity is the Prince's shadow—the memory of a conqueror who was never crowned.

data.title: The Prince's Shadow Timer (Pereshi)
data.body: Tracks the return of the Forgotten Ashaani Prince. Advances when: a Pereshi oath is broken, a Flame-Keeper dies, the Prince's name is spoken aloud, or the GM spends 2 SB to represent a crack in the archive's seal. At 4, the Prince's shadow appears in mirrors. At 8, the Prince manifests as a ghostly presence. The party must reseal him, bargain with him, or find a new shadow to bind.

data.title: The Ukwe (Sekogo)
data.body: The Speaking Tree of Sekogo, a baobab so old its bark is carved with a thousand names. It speaks in the voices of the dead, and it remembers every broken promise. The ninth root never stops growing—it searches for the name that was erased. The Ukwe's roots extend into the Crimson Valley, where the Lethai-ar bury their dead Marks.

data.title: The Leopard Society (Sekogo)
data.body: Masked hunters who restore balance in Sekogo. They hunt oath-breakers, slavers, and those who break the deepest taboos. Their masks are carved wood, painted with symbols of lineage; a cracked mask means a broken taboo. The Leopard King leads them—a spirit with no mask, its face a leopard's, its eyes human. The ninth hunter who follows it never returns.

data.title: The Crimson Valley (Lethai-ar)
data.body: A deep jungle rift of red stone, guarded by the Lethai-ar. Silk bridges span the gorges, woven from spider-sap and oath-hair. The web-law is unwritten; every warden carries a different clause in memory. The valley is a creature—a sleeping serpent whose spine is the canyon walls, whose heart is the rust-colored river. Tagline: 'The bridge remembers every step. The silk knows every promise.'

data.title: The Web-Law (Crimson Valley)
data.body: The unwritten legal code of the Crimson Valley. Each Lethai-ar warden carries a different clause in memory; together, they form a complete web. To cross a bridge, a traveler must answer a question about the web-law. The answer changes with each warden. The ninth clause is unwritten—it is the warden's own secret.

data.title: The Gallow's Bell (Patron)
data.body: A patron of justice and judgment, cold and impartial. It weighs all accounts in time, measuring action against consequence. Its followers are judges, notaries, and those who speak final words. The Bell does not rage; it tolls. To call upon the Bell is to bind oneself to the gravity of truth, where even silence is judged.

data.title: The Confessor Beneath the Bell
data.body: A patron of burden and exchange, the sin-eater who consumes guilt so that others may be light. He waits in places where guilt gathers—under church spires, in confessionals long abandoned, in the echo of unspoken sins. Each confession is a transaction: your burden for his silence, your pain for his weight. To follow him is to understand that sin does not vanish—it migrates.

data.title: The Pale Shepherd (Patron)
data.body: A patron of passage and melancholic wisdom, the guide of transitions. It walks the seam between life and death, joy and sorrow, memory and forgetting. It offers safe conduct through liminal space for a price paid in memory, feeling, or fate. Its followers are death-doulas, grief counselors, and those who have lost so much that they have become experts in loss.

data.title: The Silent Choir (Patron)
data.body: A patron of restraint and protective omission, the keeper of unspoken truths. It teaches that some knowledge wounds more than it heals, and that mercy is sometimes silence. Its followers are confessors, archivists, and therapists who carry burdens so that others may walk free. The word not spoken is a shield. The secret kept is a kindness.

data.title: The Sealed Gate (Patron)
data.body: A patron of thresholds and containment, the guardian of boundaries. It stands where realities meet, embodying the sacred power of borders and separation. Its followers are wardens, exorcists, and philosophers of separation who believe some things must be kept apart for the world to function. To serve it is to become a wall given will.

data.title: Morag the Hag (Patron)
data.body: A patron of faerie bargains and hidden costs, the weaver of unspoken prices. She is the grandmother who offers exactly what you need, the forest crone with a perfect solution, the crossroads dweller who makes dreams come true for a price that only reveals itself once the road bends back. Her bargains are never unfair—only incomplete.

data.title: Palinode (Queen of Encores)
data.body: A patron of performance and rapture, the queen of unfinished art. She is the refrain that refuses to end, the song that never dies, the encore that commands. Her followers are performers who risk everything for a single, perfect moment. The art that is never finished is the art that never dies.

data.title: Aveh (Rider Behind the Storm)
data.body: A patron of freedom and erasure, the storm-shadow that offers liberty at the cost of belonging. They are the faceless rider at the horizon's edge, neither man nor woman, both and neither. To travel with Aveh is to taste unchained freedom—and to risk being erased by the storm that follows. They are the patron of the outcast, the non-conforming, and the forgotten.

data.title: The Unbroken Way (Patron)
data.body: A patron of balance and control, the path of perfect equilibrium. It does not speak—it listens. It is the pause between breaths, the space between thoughts, the stillness at the heart of motion. Its followers are mediators, guardians, and seekers of equilibrium. The blade that is not drawn cannot be broken. The hand that is not clenched cannot be bound.

data.title: Khemesh (The Abyssal Maw)
data.body: A patron of depths and eldritch terror, the hunger beneath the seas. He is the classic warlock's patron: distant, vast, and utterly indifferent to mortal morality. To serve Khemesh is to accept that the universe is cold, that the deep does not hate—it simply consumes. He is Raéyn's son, the kraken who embodies the crushing inevitability of the ocean's dark heart.

data.title: Raéyn (Mistress of the Sea)
data.body: A patron of tides and change, the tempestuous goddess of the sea. She is mother to all who sail, her voice the wind that fills sails and her moods the storms that test every mariner. Her heart is torn by her son Khemesh, the Kraken of the Depths. Where Raéyn brings change and opportunity, Khemesh brings the final, inescapable pressure that grinds all things to nothing.

data.title: Mor'iraath (The Destroyer)
data.body: A patron of annihilation and inferno, the demon of absolute destruction. He delights in the perfect moment of combustion, when something that was becomes something that never will be again. His followers become agents of finality, wielding flame that leaves no trace, no remains, and no possibility of reconstruction. Ash is the only inheritance.

data.title: The Narethi (Deep Desert Felids)
data.body: Cat-people who dwell in the Sunken Courts beneath the Deep Desert. They are ruled by the Father of Resonance, who interprets the dream of the Unburied—a crystalline Sorcerer-King who drew the power of the Unsunken Well into itself. They follow two dreams: the Unbroken Way (calm) and the Riven Path (rage). They trade with the Fhara at boundary stones, leaving offerings of salt and dried dates.

data.title: The Sunken Courts (Narethi)
data.body: A network of subterranean chambers beneath the Deep Desert, carved from ancient salt and basalt. The entrance is a sinkhole that smells of ozone. Visitors are blindfolded and led through nine switchbacks. The Courts are lit by phosphorescent crystals that pulse faintly, as if breathing. At the heart of the Courts lies the Unburied—a crystalline Sorcerer-King who dreams of two things: the Unbroken Way and the Riven Path.

data.title: The Unburied (Narethi)
data.body: The crystalline Sorcerer-King of the Narethi, fused into a throne of petrified wood. Its body is salt-crusted glass; its mind is shattered into fragments, each dreaming a different dream. It drew the power of the Unsunken Well into itself—and the thing that slept beneath the well with it. Its dreams leak through crystals that Narethi cut and polish. It is a lock, not a prisoner. Beneath it, something else sleeps.

data.title: The Unbroken Way (Narethi Dream)
data.body: One of the two dreams of the Unburied. It is the dream of calm—the regret that it had not found another way. A world where control, discipline, and restraint could have saved its people without destroying them. Followers learn stillness, precision, and the open hand that redirects force rather than meeting it. The Father of Resonance interprets this dream.

data.title: The Riven Path (Narethi Dream)
data.body: One of the two dreams of the Unburied. It is the dream of rage—the fury that desired to break the thing that forced its hand. A world where power is seized, chains are shattered, and oppression is answered with annihilation. Followers learn passion, liberation, and the closed fist that breaks what it cannot bend. It is the same name as the patron of the same name—a syncretic connection.

data.title: The Unsunken Well (Narethi)
data.body: A font of psionic energy with no known bottom, located beneath the Sunken Courts. The Unburied reached into it and pulled, drawing the well's power into itself—and the thing that slept beneath the well with it. The well went dry, and the Great Silence killed most of the Narethi. The survivors woke with no memory of who they had been.

data.title: Thin Places
data.body: Locations where the boundary between the waking world and the Ways Between is unusually permeable. Crossing is not a matter of ritual or intent—it is a matter of being in the wrong place at the wrong angle. A wrong step, a miscounted breath, a name spoken at the wrong hour. Thin places are the cracks where the Hollow's attention seeps through.

data.title: The Long Mile of Temptation
data.body: A path in the Ways Between where the road stretches differently for each traveler. It is Vice's testing ground, where the Hollow's Oath-Keeper waits at the halfway mark. Those who walk it must face the choices they have not made and the debts they have not paid. It is a place of judgment, not a place of travel.

data.title: The Thirteenth Stone
data.body: A warm stone in the deepest layer of the Ways Between. It is Ikasha's Seal—the path reveals its true destination here. The stone whispers a promise you made to yourself and broke. Beneath it, Ikasha dreams of freedom. Her nightmares seep upward, infecting the layers above.

data.title: Varnek Karn (Death's Negotiator)
data.body: A patron of bargains with the departed, the broker who speaks across the veil. He dwells in the gray between life and death, mediating disputes between living and dead. His servants practice post-mortem diplomacy: they negotiate with spirits as equals. The dead are patient and rarely generous—but they are honest. To serve him is to understand that death cancels all ledgers.

data.title: The Unquiet Host
data.body: A temporary spectral warband summoned by a follower of Varnek Karn. It is a Cap 3 Follower that can Assist (+3 dice to a combat or intimidation roll) or take Independent Action (Scout & Signal, Distract & Draw). It is vulnerable to salt, bells, and consecrated ground. When it departs, the dead demand their due: Obligation or a Memorial Rite.

data.title: Beast-kin (Valewood)
data.body: The descendants of the Genesis Vats—elf and beast combined, spirit and stone fused. They are not a single species but a loose alliance of animal-aspected beings. They have Scent Memory (+1 die to track by smell), Parliament Oath (ask a local animal one question), and Claw or Fang (unarmed strikes deal Harm 1). They are the empire's unfinished business.

data.title: The Genesis Vats (Valewood)
data.body: Deep beneath the Amber Ziggurat, the Lethai-thora's failed laboratories. Here, elf and beast were combined to create the perfect guardian. The vats still hum, and the beast-kin who survived do not speak of what they saw. The Genesis Keeper (a ghost) still tries to finish the equation for a thousand years. It is almost complete.

data.title: The Amber Ziggurat (Valewood)
data.body: A ruin caught mid-construction for a thousand years. The workers are statues of amber; their eyes follow you. Beneath it, the Genesis Vats still hum. It is the heart of the Valewood's forgotten empire, where the Lethai-thora built their weapons and sealed their guilt. The Shardwrights guard its secrets.

data.title: The Hazel Queen (Valewood)
data.body: Sovereign of the Hazel Court, a Lethai-al ruler in leaf and law. She has never spoken a lie—she has never needed to. Her court sings of a door that should stay closed. She is the forest's voice, a title that passes from dryad to dryad. The current Queen is not a dryad—she is a ghost, the last survivor of the empire that fell beneath the leaves.

data.title: The Alder King (Valewood)
data.body: Sovereign of the Twilit Court, a ruler in shadow and promise. His crown is a noose of thorns; he wears it proudly. He knows what came through the door. He will not say. He is the forest's warden, a title passed from fallen empire to fallen empire. The current King is a Lethai-ar who was born in the year the last empire fell. He has not aged since.

data.title: Star-Roads (Valewood)
data.body: Ancient paths between worlds, cracked and phasing. They hum with geometries that twist the unwary into yesterday. A Star-Road Shard is a pale flagstone that hums when trod in sequence—the sequence is always incomplete. The missing step is the one you hesitate to take. The Shardwrights repair them, but the empire's ghosts still patrol them.

data.title: The Lethai-al (Valewood)
data.body: The true wood elves, those who remain when the tower falls. They do not walk the high roads; they mend them from below, speaking to roots instead of stars. Their elders are oaks, their children are saplings, and their grievances outlast stone. They keep no scrolls and sign no contracts, yet nothing is given without expectation. A meal shared is a shield-pledge. A path shown is a future claimed.

data.title: The Lethai-thora (Valewood)
data.body: The high elf archivists and sorcerers who served the old fey courts. They fled east when the courts fell, crossing the mountains with armfuls of scrolls. In Sihai, they taught the tribes to write contracts instead of drawing blood. Now they dwell in hidden pavilions, preserving 'forgotten ledgers' that record what the Mandate prefers to forget. Each secret they preserve erases a piece of themselves.

data.title: The Fledging of the Empire (Lethai-thora Origin)
data.body: When the Valewood's fey courts crumbled, a caravan of Lethai-thora refugees crossed the eastern passes. They found warring clans along the Sihon River and taught them to write disputes on clay. A generation later, the first emperor rose—a man who had learned his letters from a Lethai-thora tutor. He built his capital around the archive, and the Lethai-thora became the empire's memory.

data.title: Asset Crafter
data.body: Reduce the XP cost to acquire a new Asset by 1 per tier (Minor: 4→3 XP; Standard: 8→6 XP; Major: 12→9 XP; Artifact: 16→12 XP). Also reduce the required downtime by half (rounded up, minimum 1 day). This talent does not apply to Assets gained through narrative events without XP cost.

data.title: Stabilize Weave
data.body: Once per session, you may cancel a single Story Beat generated by your own casting (Free Casting roll). The Weave does not forget; it merely postpones the receipt. Use this when the consequences would be catastrophic. Use it sparingly otherwise.

data.title: Threadweaver's Patience
data.body: You may delay the resolution of a spell for up to one exchange. During the delay, you maintain the tags in your mind but do not release them. The Weave holds its breath. If you are interrupted during the delay, the spell fails and you suffer Backlash as if you had rolled a miss. Useful for ambushes. Dangerous for the impatient.

data.title: Signature Spell
data.body: Choose a single spell you have cast successfully at least three times. When you cast that spell, you gain +1 die on the roll. Additionally, the first time you cast it in a scene, you may ignore the first Story Beat generated by ones (if any). The Weave recognizes repetition. It does not applaud, but it does not interrupt.

data.title: Echo Recall
data.body: Once per session, after a failed casting, you may immediately attempt the same spell again with a +1 die. The Weave permits a second draft. The Backlash for the second attempt is applied regardless of success or failure. Lysandra used this talent twice. Both times, the second draft was worse than the first. Your experience may differ.

data.title: Elemental Rebuke
data.body: Requires Elemental Focus. When an enemy casts a spell of your chosen element within Near range, you may attempt to twist the Weave against them. Roll a contested Arcana check. On success, the enemy's spell resolves as you choose—redirected, weakened, or reflected. On failure, you suffer the Backlash instead. The Weave does not appreciate interference, but it respects audacity.

data.title: Safe Harbour
data.body: When you cast a [WARD] or [DEFEND] spell, you may extend its protection to one adjacent ally without increasing the DV. The Weave does not distinguish between your skin and theirs, provided you ask politely.

data.title: Practiced Caster
data.body: Reduce the DV of any cantrip (one-tag spell) by 1, to a minimum of 1. A candle that lights itself is not a miracle. It is practice.

data.title: Catastrophe Insurance
data.body: Once per campaign, when you would suffer a Catastrophic Backlash, you may instead convert it to a Major Backlash. The Weave accepts this substitution because you have paid in advance—with a memory, a name, or a promise. Lysandra keeps this in her ledger in case.

data.title: Burning
data.body: Ignite, heat, combustion, smoke. The classic fire tag.

data.title: Freezing
data.body: Ice, slowing, brittle shatter, cold. The frost tag.

data.title: Storm
data.body: Lightning, shock, arc, thunder. The lightning tag.

data.title: Stone
data.body: Walls, spikes, tremors, armor. The earth tag.

data.title: Wave
data.body: Crushing water, currents, pressure. The water tag.

data.title: Wind
data.body: Levitation, gusts, deflection, push/pull. The air tag.

data.title: Force
data.body: Kinetic power, shields, blasts, telekinesis. The raw force tag.

data.title: Area
data.body: Cone, circle, corridor, zone effect. Expands a spell to affect multiple targets.

data.title: Strike
data.body: Single target precision. Focused damage or effect.

data.title: Wall
data.body: Barrier or blockade. Creates a physical or magical wall.

data.title: Bind
data.body: Restrain, hold, suspend, entangle. Restrains a target.

data.title: Dispel
data.body: Suppress magic, unravel ongoing effects. Counters or removes magic.

data.title: Veil
data.body: Conceal, blur, illusion, silence. Hides or obscures.

data.title: Scry
data.body: Reveal hidden, see distance, read traces. Distant viewing.

data.title: Memory
data.body: Erase, alter, restore memories. Mind magic – handle with care.

data.title: Command
data.body: Compel a short action (one word). High risk, high reward.

data.title: Fear
data.body: Panic, flee, break morale. Area morale break.

data.title: HEAL
data.body: Close wounds, restore flesh, reduce Harm 1. Restoration magic.

data.title: Purify
data.body: Remove poison, corruption, disease. Cleansing magic.

data.title: Strengthen
data.body: Enhance body, armor, senses (temporary). Buff magic.

data.title: Waken
data.body: Counter sleep, paralysis, stun. Rouses a stunned creature.

data.title: Beast
data.body: Speak with or influence animals. Animal communication.

data.title: Sense
data.body: Detect presence of a named tag/element. Detection magic.

data.title: Reveal
data.body: Unveil hidden, glamoured, or invisible things. Pierces illusions.

data.title: Light
data.body: Create illumination (glow, torch-bright). Simple and safe.

data.title: Shadow
data.body: Deepen darkness, hide edges, obscure. Darkness magic.

data.title: Silence
data.body: Suppress sound in zone or on target. Sound muffling.

data.title: Protect
data.body: Reduce/deflect next harm (Armor 1). Defensive magic.

data.title: Counter
data.body: Interrupt a casting/ritual in its window. Reactive dispel.

data.title: Bless
data.body: Grant favourable tag (luck, favor, ward-key). Friendly affliction.

data.title: Leap
data.body: Jump far, blink across short space (Near). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Fold
data.body: Short-range teleport, vanish-reappear (Far). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Gate
data.body: Long distance passage, open/close path. Dangerous tag.

data.title: Gravity
data.body: Crush, lift, suspend, walk on walls/ceiling. Dangerous tag.

data.title: Create
data.body: Manifest mundane matter briefly (1 scene). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Summon
data.body: Call a being or construct. Dangerous tag.

data.title: Transmute
data.body: Turn one thing into another (temporary). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Animate
data.body: Make objects act with intent (1 scene). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Reflect
data.body: Turn next targeted effect back on its source. Dangerous tag.

data.title: Store
data.body: Bank 1–2 successes in a vessel (once). Dangerous tag.

data.title: Curse
data.body: Attach hostile tag/timer to target. Dangerous tag.

data.title: High Cantor
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path, Tier III. Allows you to weave Standard Rites into instant, powerful Songs. Each such casting marks your Corruption Timer, but the effects are immediate. Cost: 18 XP.

data.title: Patron's Dedication
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path. You bind your voice to a single Patron. Your Corruption timer is always keyed to that Patron—it never resets to a different Patron's table when you bloom. Singing a Song of any other Patron worsens your Position by one step. Cost: 4 XP.

data.title: Resonant Performance
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path. Gain +1 die when performing for an audience of 5 or more. Cost: 3 XP.

data.title: Song Weaver
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path. Combine two compatible Songs for +1 Effect. Two Songs are compatible if they share a thematic tag or are from the same Patron. Sing both as a single action; resolve the Performance roll once. Cost: 4 XP.

data.title: Steady Voice
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path. Passive. When you Push a Song, you may choose to mark 1 additional Fatigue instead of marking a Corruption segment (once per scene). You cannot use this talent if your Corruption timer is already full. This talent gives low-Spirit Cantors an emergency buffer at the cost of greater exhaustion. Cost: 2 XP.

data.title: Embraced Corruption
data.body: Prerequisite: Cantor's Path, Tier II+. You have learned to treat the bloom not as disease but as evolution. When you voluntarily fill your Corruption Timer through Resonant Rites (not by Pushing), you may choose your corruption trait rather than accepting a random result. You may Push Songs without marking Fatigue once per session. After seven blooms, gain the Fugal Self: +1 die to all Performance rolls, but each morning test Spirit+Resolve (DV 3) or your Corruption controls your body for the first scene. Cost: 12 XP.

data.title: Threshold Sense
data.body: Prerequisite: Witchcraft (Craft of the Hedge). Gain +1 die to detect hidden thresholds, boundaries, or debts in any scene. This is a passive ability. Cost: 3 XP.

data.title: Promise Keeper
data.body: Prerequisite: Witchcraft. When you bind a promise with a Hedge Gift or Quick Working, the Promise Timer starts at 6 segments instead of 4. You may also spend 1 Boon to clear one segment from any Promise Timer you have set. Cost: 5 XP.

data.title: Weaver's Resolve
data.body: Prerequisite: Witchcraft. When you would mark Identity Strain, you may instead mark 2 Fatigue (once per scene). The strain of touching your own identity is deferred to your body. Cost: 6 XP.

data.title: Kinetic Momentum
data.body: You can use the force of your attacks to propel yourself. When you make a successful melee attack, you may immediately move one range band (Close→Near or Near→Close) without provoking opportunity attacks. You may not use this talent more than once per round. Requires Melee 2+, Athletics 2+.

data.title: Uncanny Dodge
data.body: You are always treated as having Partial Cover against ranged attacks, even in the open (the Weave twists around you). When you take the Defend action against a ranged attack, improve Position by one step. Requires Elusive Dodge, Wits 3+.

data.title: Light Fingers
data.body: Active, once per scene. When you attempt to lift a small object (purse, key, letter, seal) from a person or desk, treat your first Stealth or Subterfuge roll as Position +1. No one notices until it is already in your sleeve.
data.quote: No one notices until it is already in your sleeve.

data.title: The Unlocked Window
data.body: Passive. When infiltrating a structure you have cased for at least an hour, ignore one security obstacle (locked door, patrolled corridor, guard dog) per session. Describe how you already prepared for it.

data.title: Silk Palms
data.body: Active. When you bribe or gift a minor official, you gain a temporary String: Bought Silence. Once, you may activate this String to reduce DV by 1 on a Petition or Broker action involving that official. The String is consumed afterward.

data.title: Always Another Exit
data.body: Active, once per session. When you are cornered or a heist goes wrong, you may declare that you prepared an escape route earlier. Describe it plausibly (rope out a window, a bribed guard, a secret door). The GM may impose a cost — a dropped item, a witness, a future debt — but you get out.

data.title: The Forger's Eye
data.body: Active. You can copy any handwriting, seal, or signature with uncanny accuracy. When you attempt to forge a document, roll Wits + Craft (DV 3 for simple, 4–5 for complex). On a hit, create a Forged credential. On a partial, the forgery holds for one scene, after which it may be detected.

data.title: Crowd Veil
data.body: Active. You vanish into crowds. When in a populated area (market, festival, dock), you may roll Stealth vs. DV 3 to become Hidden in plain sight. Pursuers suffer −1 die to find you until you act conspicuously.

data.title: The Velvet Glove
data.body: Active, once per session. You have cultivated a network of informants, fence contacts, and corrupted clerks. You may declare that a minor NPC (a servant, a dockworker, a scribe) owes you a favor. They provide a specific service: unlock a door, delay a patrol, deliver a message. The GM may dictate a cost — the NPC will later need help, or their favor expires after use.

data.title: Master of Misdirection
data.body: Active. When you are discovered during a crime, you may spend 1 Boon to redirect suspicion to another person or faction. Roll Deception vs. DV 4. On a hit, the heat shifts; on a miss, you gain Exposure +1 and the target becomes hostile.

data.title: Ghost Heist
data.body: Active, once per arc. You may commit a crime that is never solved — not because you are perfect, but because the evidence points nowhere. After a successful heist, you may declare that no traceable evidence remains; the GM cannot use Social SB to retroactively implicate you from that scene. Cost: you must accept a permanent Reputation: Whispers tag — some will always suspect you, even without proof.

data.body: Bow, crossbow, sling, thrown weapon, or firearm. Close: -2d (the loose-a-clean-shot penalty; base rules call this Desperate Position instead — see Ranged & Tempo), Near: +2d, Far: +1d. Weight (Light/Medium/Heavy) sets Tempo — Light is Fast (move and shoot), Medium is Standard (move or shoot, or Aim for +1d/+1 Effect), Heavy is Slow (load one round, shoot the next). data.title: Range Bands (Extended)
data.body: House rule used by this table's combat tracker and VTT: the base 3-band Close/Near/Far scale is split into five bands for finer-grained weapon reach — Close (knife/grapple distance, well within arm's reach), Medium (striking distance of a one-handed weapon — the tracker's internal name for what the core rules call "Near"), Reach (striking distance of a two-handed weapon — only Heavy melee weapons and Reach-tagged weapons threaten this band), Far (beyond melee range — missile-weapon distance), and Absent (beyond missile range — functionally gone, requires a scene change to close). The GM sets range between combatants; players pick the range they were told before rolling so the table's dice bonus applies. See Light/Medium/Heavy/Ranged Weapon entries for the bonus at each band.

data.title: X-Card / Veils
data.body: A safety tool: any player can call the X-Card at any time to stop a scene that's making them uncomfortable, no questions asked. In this toolkit it's a floating button on every screen (also Ctrl+Shift+X) that pauses the table — when connected to a live campaign, raising it notifies every other connected player and GM, not just the person who called it, and a resume button clears it for everyone. Lines and Veils (hard limits and soft-pedal-past-them content, set by the group during Session Zero) are shown alongside the pause so everyone can see what to avoid before play continues.
